name: T11c — Touch haptics
description:
Depends on: T11b.

Touch-control haptics only (native Android View path):
- Add `runtime/input/touch_haptics.*`: a host-testable policy with an injected sink. A new face-button, L/R, START/SELECT or d-pad touch-down requests exactly one short tick; analog-stick down/movement, edit drag/resize, release and slide-between-controls request none.
- `TouchOverlayView` executes the tick with `performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK)` (API 26+, respects the system touch-feedback setting), guarded by `isHapticFeedbackEnabled()`. No vibrator or disabled setting is a silent no-op.
- No time-based throttle: each distinct touch-down must survive, otherwise a rapid press is swallowed. The platform haptic API coalesces at the hardware layer; a failed/absent vibration must never throw, block input, or leave a pressed state stuck.
- Host policy tests with an injected sink: one request per button/dpad down; none for stick, edit, move, slide or release; disabled/absent sink is a no-op; five rapid downs produce five requests; a throwing sink is caught and later presses still work.
- Physical phone QA: observe a short tick on every button/dpad press; disable system touch feedback and confirm silence while input still works. The x86_64 emulator proves only the no-op path.
- Explicitly exclude gamepad rumble, `sceRumble`, and battle haptics; those are deferred to T13/M5.

Reference set: Yakumo's MIT `touch_action::take_haptics` and `platform/android_jni.cpp` `haptic_tick` are the behavioral pattern; Android `HapticFeedbackConstants`/`performHapticFeedback` and the system touch-feedback setting are the platform contract. PPSSPP/Dolphin vibration behavior is behavioral only (GPL; no code copied). Adjust Yakumo's swipe/D-pad-direction feedback to the chosen new-touch-down-only scope.

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): tests observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "performHapticFeedback" --extension java`; `gh search code "HapticFeedbackConstants" --extension java`; `gh search code "isHapticFeedbackEnabled" --extension java`; `gh search code "VibrationEffect.createOneShot" --extension java`; `gh search issues "Android touch haptics"`.

Device validation: see `android/AGENTS.md` — emulator is for initial bring-up; physical arm64 phone QA is required at sprint end and recorded in `docs/qa/`. Reproducible emulator: `scripts/android/emulator.sh`.
result:
T11c complete (implementation df27849, QA 91578b5).

- runtime/input/touch_haptics.*: host-testable policy with an injected sink. A new face-button, L/R, START/SELECT or d-pad down calls the sink exactly once; the stick, slide/move, edit gestures and release never do. No time-based throttle, so a genuine rapid press is not swallowed; a missing, disabled or throwing sink is a no-op and cannot change input state.
- TouchOverlay::touch_down now returns the hit control; the JNI bridge returns the policy result. The Android View uses performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK) after checking Settings.System.HAPTIC_FEEDBACK_ENABLED; a disabled setting or missing vibrator is silent while input still works. Debug logs name performed/disabled.
- Red-first: tests/input/touch_haptics_tests.cpp and tests/test_touch_haptics.py were added before touch_haptics.* existed; configure failed on the missing source, then the policy went green. Contracts cover the control table, one tick per down, five rapid downs, disabled/absent/throwing sinks and TouchOverlay hit results.
- Device QA on M2102K1AC (arm64, API 34), app df27849: JNI/Java logged touch_haptic performed=true; dumpsys vibrator_manager recorded com.gungnir.recomp, usage TOUCH, performHapticFeedback/View#performHapticFeedback, TEXTURE_TICK, 24ms. L/R/START/SELECT plus four d-pad directions counted 8/8; five rapid Cross taps counted 5/5. Stick drag and edit drag/resize counted 0. With haptic_feedback_enabled=0 the View logged touch_haptic_disabled and no effect appeared; re-enabling restored the tick. Manual physical feel passed. Report docs/qa/2026-10-31-t11c-touch-haptics.md.
- Gates: full suite 136/136 OK; Android clean-checkout APK gate passes; repository_check PASS (323 files). The x86_64 emulator exposes a virtual vibrator so it exercised the tick path; no-vibrator no-op is covered by the absent-sink host contract and performHapticFeedback returning false.

References: TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, pinned b61852a) touch_action haptics and android_jni haptic_tick as behavioral patterns (no code copied); Android HapticFeedbackConstants/performHapticFeedback and Settings.System.HAPTIC_FEEDBACK_ENABLED contract; PPSSPP/Dolphin vibration behavior behavioral only (GPL, no code or assets copied). Gaps: gamepad rumble, sceRumble and battle haptics are deferred to T13/M5; consolidated T11 gate is T11e.

name: Research first — T16b
description:
Discover how reference emulators implement stretch/crop/fit display layouts, then record the decision before any code.

## Additional PSP references (2026-11-01)

Source: two PSP static recompilations, behavioral only.

**Both PSP ports avoid stretching the whole frame.** BasedYuki/the-3rd-
birthday-recomp widens the FOV and squeezes only the HUD into a centred 16:9
area, clipping squeezed HUD draws to the PSP screen; highcmd/chinatown-wars-
psp-recomp fits and letterboxes the 480:272 frame even in fullscreen, raising
internal resolution with `render_scale` instead. Stretch as a whole-frame
mode is a PPSSPP option (`bDisplayStretch`), not something either PSP port
ships as the default.

**Chinatown Wars `hud_scale`** (100/75/50) shrinks HUD elements towards
their corner or edge, leaving full-screen menus at their size
(`docs/OPTIONS.md`, `runtime/src/settings.h`). That is the "use more screen
without distortion" answer the PSP ports chose; it composes with fit and
with true widescreen, and it is an alternative to crop for this title.

**Implication for T16b.** Keep stretch opt-in and default to fit. Offer crop
only with a warning about clipped HUD/subtitles (the 3rd Birthday and this
title both draw UI at the edges), and consider HUD scaling as a fourth
policy later. The presentation policy stays host-only either way.

## Retraction 2026-11-03

The "touch targets drift" claim is wrong: the touch overlay has no guest-pixel mapping. `TouchOverlay::set_viewport` (`runtime/input/touch_overlay.cpp:80`) takes window size plus safe-area insets and hit-tests/draws controls in window space from normalized placements (`TouchOverlayView.java:177`, `:228`); no tap is converted to a guest coordinate. The real T16b input question is whether controls should be anchored to the presented image rect instead of the window, so they do not float over black bars. See the T16b task description.
result:
Research complete; no code written. Question: what is the cheapest correct
way to fill the display, and what does it break?

**This is presentation, not rendering.** The guest still produces a 480x272
(1.765:1) frame. "Fill" only changes how that rectangle maps to the
surface, so no GE/projection change and no snapshot identity change.

**PPSSPP (the closest reference for PSP content).** Its display layout is
exactly this policy: a `bDisplayStretch` checkbox (disabled when integer
scaling is on), `fDisplayAspectRatio`, `bDisplayIntegerScale` and
`bDisplayCropTo16x9` (`UI/DisplayLayoutScreen.cpp:283-296`;
`GPU/Common/PresentationCommon.cpp:145-200` applies the aspect adjust and
crop). Stretch is a user choice, not the default, because it distorts.
Refs: hrydgard/ppsspp `UI/DisplayLayoutScreen.cpp`,
`GPU/Common/PresentationCommon.cpp`.

**DuckStation.** Keeps projection-level widescreen (`WidescreenHack`) and
display aspect selection separate, and warns/overrides when a title has its
own widescreen patch (`src/core/imgui_overlays.cpp`, `src/core/cheats.cpp`).
That separation is the one proposed here.
Refs: stenzek/duckstation `src/core/imgui_overlays.cpp`,
`src/core/cheats.cpp`.

**Local anchor.** `fit_viewport` (`runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp:174`) is
the single fit policy; `scale_scissor_to_extent` (line 193) maps guest
scissors into the fitted rect and both are used at lines 1724/1737.
`present_guest_frame` (`android/app/src/main/cpp/main.cpp:242`) only
forwards draws, and the touch overlay viewport is set at
`main.cpp:503` (`TouchOverlayView_nativeViewport`) — that mapping must use
the same policy or touch targets drift.

**Numbers.** A 19.5:9 phone is 2.167:1. Stretch = ~23% horizontal
magnification (or 15% vertical squash). Crop-to-fill = uniform scale to
cover, losing ~20% of the frame height (~10% top and bottom) on 19.5:9;
this title draws HUD and subtitles near the edges, and FMV dialogue boxes
would be clipped. Integer scaling cannot fill.

**Quality.** Nearest sampling at a non-integer factor shimmers on scrolling
text; linear softens 1x pixel art. PPSSPP exposes both and defaults to
linear-ish scaling at non-integer factors.

Decision: one presentation policy enum {fit (default, unchanged), stretch,
crop} in `fit_viewport` + scissor mapping, mirrored by touch input; no
guest or snapshot state changes. No third-party code copied (AGENTS #0).

name: T15 — Host save states: snapshot and restore a running session
description:
Host save states so a device or host run can resume at a known guest point instead of
replaying the prologue (~10-15 min) for every new crash deeper in the game.

**Why.** The new-game path now reaches the first battle; every further HLE gap costs a
full replay. Manual QA and crash triage need a deterministic resume point.

**Scope.** Serialize and restore one GameSession:
- Guest RAM (32 MiB) and EDRAM (2 MiB) byte-for-byte; scratchpad too if it is live.
- The runner's CPU context (pc, gpr, fpr/VFPU, hi/lo, branch-delay state) and the
  thread table with every thread's saved context, status and wait state.
- Kernel objects by stable identity: semaphores, event flags, mutexes, VPLs, FPLs,
  msgpipes, VTimers, alarms, callbacks, interrupts, plus the virtual clock so timers
  keep their absolute deadlines.
- HLE-owned state: open file descriptors and their positions, async op staging,
  savedata/utility status machines, audio channel reservations, ATRAC IDs, GE list
  registry, module registry.
- Audio/mixer and GPU caches are NOT serialized: they are derived. Restore must
  rebuild them (textures re-decode from guest RAM, mixer reset with a named bump) and
  the snapshot must say so, not silently pretend audio continuity.
- Format: versioned header (magic, version, AOT corpus identity hash, guest image
  identity, session config) plus section table with lengths and a payload hash.
  Truncated, corrupt, wrong-corpus or wrong-version snapshots fail with a named error;
  never a partial restore.

**Non-goals.** No emulator-format interoperability, no clean-room reimplementation of an
existing savestate format (AGENTS #0); if the research finds a suitable existing format,
use it out-of-process rather than writing one.

**Red-first tests.**
- Round trip: snapshot -> restore into a fresh session -> the next N dispatches produce a
  byte-identical dispatch trace and identical guest RAM/EDRAM checksum.
- Determinism: two snapshots taken at the same dispatch count are byte-identical.
- Rejection: truncated section, flipped payload byte, wrong corpus hash and wrong version
  each fail with their named error and leave the previous session untouched.
- Kernel timers: a snapshot taken with a pending VTimer fires at the same virtual time
  after restore.
- Audio/GE rebuild: restore with a stubbed sink and empty texture caches runs without
  retaining state from the snapshot.

**Evidence.** Host round-trip report with timings and snapshot size; device snapshot at
the first battle, restore and screenshot comparison; no proprietary content in the repo.

**Guardrails.** A snapshot embeds guest RAM, i.e. game data. Snapshots are never committed,
never packaged, never uploaded; they live in app-private storage and under gitignored
`build/qa/` on the host, like the disc image. No hidden failures: a failed save or restore
is a named error at the call site.

Decomposition (dex): T15a (e3ib7rpp) is the implementation subtask — snapshot container, guest RAM/EDRAM, CPU and thread table, kernel objects and timers, HLE state, restore path, host and Android surfaces. Its research step is `Research first — T15a` (r9q5jqf0). Split it into further lettered subtasks only if it grows past one reviewable change; each new subtask then starts with its own reference-discovery step and records the references used.

**Subtasks.** `Research first — T15a` (r9q5jqf0) records the reference answers and is
complete; `T15a — Implement snapshot and restore` (e3ib7rpp) is the implementation and is
blocked by it. dex enforces incomplete subtasks on completion, so this task cannot close
before T15a does (blocker relations on their own are advisory in v0.16.0, see
dcramer/dex#134).

## Research findings (2026-11-01)

Source: PPSSPP `Core/SaveState.cpp`, `Core/HLE/sceKernel.cpp`,
`Core/HLE/sceAudio.cpp`, `Common/Serialize/Serializer.h` (behavioral only; no
code copied — see `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`, T15 section).

**Section list and order.** Quiesce first (utility IO, SAS mixer, async IO,
flush pending GPU drawing), then: RAM/EDRAM -> virtual clock -> memory stick ->
CPU context -> HLE module state -> kernel objects, interrupts, kernel memory,
threading, alarms, VTimers, event flags, mailboxes, modules, msgpipes, mutexes,
semaphores -> open file descriptors **last** (kernel object destruction may
close files). Drop MMIO and media-engine sections: this title uses neither.
Savedata lives on the virtual memory stick, so the snapshot does not contain
it and must say so.

**Timer deadlines are absolute.** The virtual clock is restored with the
objects so a pending VTimer/alarm fires at the same virtual time after load;
relative-only timer state is wrong.

**Derived state is rebuilt.** Audio channels are HLE state and *are* saved
(reserved, sample address/count, volumes, format, remaining samples, parked
waiting thread/address/volumes). The mixer/AAudio stream and the GPU texture
caches are not: reset the mixer with a named bump and let textures re-decode
from restored guest RAM. The reference flushes GPU drawing before saving and
resets caches on load.

**Object identity.** UIDs are restored verbatim; nothing is renumbered. Our
SceUID-keyed maps serialize as-is, provided ID allocation stays deterministic
and load rejects duplicates.

**Container.** PPSSPP's chunk writer is Dolphin-derived GPL code without a
public spec. We define our own minimal TLV: magic, version, corpus/config
identity, per-section tag + length, trailing payload hash. No existing format
is copied or reimplemented (AGENTS #0).

**Failure modes.** Reject on corpus hash, config or version mismatch; verify
each section hash; write atomically (temp + rename); never leave a half-restored
session. Mirror the reference's "on failed load, keep nothing".

**Relevance to the current blocker.** The pre-battle stall is the frame thread
parked in `sceAudioOutputPannedBlocking` while other threads keep dispatching
(`docs/BRINGUP.md`). PPSSPP's audio state carries a compatibility fix for a
save that stored `waitingThread = -1`, which kept a channel busy forever, so
the first snapshot should include the audio channel fields above and the first
restore test should assert a parked waiter is either resumed or reported, never
left dangling.

Status 2026-11-01: the reference review is complete (`Research first — T15a`,
r9q5jqf0) and its answers are folded into the findings above. T15a is the first
implementation subtask and is the only one created so far; T15b and T15c are
named in the decomposition but not yet split out. No snapshot code exists yet.
result: T15 host save states proven end to end: GSNP v1 container (23 sections) + RAM/CPU/clock/threads/kernel/HLE coverage, wall_base_us + dispatch_phase continuity fixes with real-corpus equivalence (identical reports, byte-identical restores), CLI + Android Menu surfaces, docs, full suite green, manual device QA sign-off in docs/qa/2026-11-01-t15e-snapshot.md.

name: T17a.2 — Present each guest frame once, on time
description:
The present loop sleeps a fixed 16 ms and takes whatever frame is latest
(FrameQueue::take_latest replaces the pending frame and counts drops, but
nothing logs or bounds them), so presentation is neither pinned to the guest's
flip times nor proven to show every frame the guest produced.

Build a present clock: every guest flip gets a virtual timestamp and
Kernel::real_time_of already maps that to a host deadline. Present the frame
due at its deadline; never present one frame twice, never present a frame the
guest did not produce, and when the host falls behind drop the oldest with a
counted, logged event instead of hiding it behind a longer sleep.

Red-first: tests/ge/frame_pacing_tests.cpp with injected time - N guest frames
produce exactly N presents in order; a late host drops with a counted line and
never reorders; no duplicate present of one frame.
Mutation: break the deadline and confirm the scheduling contract dies for that
reason. Device acceptance is unchanged fps (pacing, not speed) with the new
counters in the periodic log.

## Visual gate

Order is visible: a deterministic present log records (frame id, present time)
for a bounded run and must show each produced frame exactly once, in order. On
the phone, two screenshots taken at known clock offsets show the expected frame
content, and the produced/presented counters match one-for-one over the run.
result:
Present pacing is implemented and measured on device (commit fc78cae).

FrameQueue now carries the host moment a frame is due: the guest flip publishes the kernel's real-time mapping of its emulated time, and the presenter waits on the queue, which publishing wakes immediately, instead of a fixed 16 ms sleep. A frame is taken once, in order and never before it exists; a host that falls behind replaces a pending frame and counts the drop, and a present past the presenter's own latency (5 ms: the presenter cannot be earlier than the frame's production and waking costs a scheduler slice) is counted as late. Both counters and the measured present cost are logged.

Host gates: tests/ge/frame_pacing_tests.cpp (6 contracts: one present per produced frame in order, no duplicate, on-time vs late threshold, the counted drop with the newest frame winning, pending deadline, and the wait returning as soon as a frame is due or in about the slice when idle), wired into test_ge_suite. GE and HLE suites plus repository_check green.

Device visual gate (M2102K1AC, battle snapshot, 40 s): 699 published, 696 presented, 3 dropped, 2 late. published = presented + dropped; the 3 drops all happen at startup and do not grow (got 3 again over a second run), the 2 late presents are one 8.7 ms deadline miss; present costs 9.5 ms average in holding mode; guest frames stay at 20 fps with draws=2834 and the battle scene unchanged in two screenshots taken 2 s apart. Startup drops are counted and visible, not hidden.

No rendering change: the boot-runner baseline PPM/JSON from T17a.1 still applies (this task touches only the host present loop).

name: T6i — Async file I/O completion (sceIoLseekAsync and friends)
description:
The T6h boot advances to 25,546 dispatches / 17 flips and stops at Missing HLE import IoFileMgrForUser::sceIoLseekAsync (NID_0x71B19E77). Implement the async IoFileMgr surface title-scoped: lseek/read/write/open/close async variants with deterministic deferred completion through the kernel (no sleeps masking races), correct SceIoStat/lseek semantics, and cancellation/error paths. Add red-first contracts in tests/hle, extend the bounded boot, and record the next blocker in docs/BRINGUP.md. Evidence: docs/BRINGUP.md 2026-10-30 T6h entry.

ABI cross-check (2026-10-30): zPSP-Dev/Zig-PSP's generated
`src/c/module/IoFileMgrForUser.zig` (MIT) documents the result-pointer
conventions for `sceIoPollAsync`, `sceIoWaitAsync`, `sceIoWaitAsyncCB` and
`sceIoGetAsyncStat`; useful when pinning T6i's asynchronous completion
contract against a second PSPSDK-derived source. It is an ABI reference only,
not an implementation to copy.

Reference leads (2026-10-30, found with `gh search issues`):
- PPSSPP #12549/#12506/#136/#153 describe the async IoFileMgr lifecycle and
  its regressions. Behavioral oracle in `Core/HLE/sceIo.cpp`: `sceIoOpenAsync`
  returns the fd directly; async read/write/lseek set a per-fd result and are
  not complete until Wait/Poll/GetAsyncStat; `sceIoWaitAsync`/`CB` write a
  64-bit result and return 0; `sceIoPollAsync` returns 1 while pending and 0
  when complete; `sceIoGetAsyncStat(fd,poll,res)` waits when poll=0 and
  reports 1 when pending; `sceIoCloseAsync` defers fd release until the
  completion wait. `sceIoLseekAsync` takes an s64 offset; bad whence returns
  INVAL; a second async op while busy returns ASYNC_BUSY. Treat as HYPOTHESIS
  until pinned by our own red-first contracts.
- wizardengineer/psprecomp #63 documents a static-recompiler async-I/O and
  scheduler race (busy-poll vs wait) to avoid when choosing the deferred
  completion policy.
- cspspemu #70 is only a stub-first discussion; do not copy that approach.
- snuri00/psp-web-recomp (MIT), `profile/host/io.cpp`, is a static-recompiler
  HLE with the same contract: async calls return immediately; WaitAsync writes
  a 64-bit result; PollAsync returns 1 while pending and completes through the
  same path; CloseAsync marks the fd closing and erases it after the wait;
  plain reads complete inline. Useful as a second implementation to diff
  against, but it completes inline rather than deferring.
- psce4all (GPL-2.0) and psprism (GPL-3.0) confirm the NID/signature table
  (`CB05F8D6` GetAsyncStat, `E23EEC33` WaitAsync, `3251EA56` PollAsync,
  `35DBD746` WaitAsyncCB, `89AA9906` OpenAsync, `FF5940B6` CloseAsync,
  `71B19E77` LseekAsync, `A0B5A7C2` ReadAsync, `0FACAB19` WriteAsync) but
  their handlers are stubs; use only as an ABI cross-check.
- jpd002/Play- (PSF player) has sync I/O only, not useful here.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.
result:
T6i complete (commit a538016).

- Implemented async IoFileMgr: open/read/write/lseek/close plus lseek32, with Wait/CB/Poll/GetAsyncStat collection. Host I/O completes synchronously, but the result is staged per descriptor and the descriptor stays busy until collected; close defers release to collection; failed async opens return a descriptor and deliver the error through Wait. Kernel error codes for busy/no-async/closed/bad-whence.
- Added reset of the IO descriptor table per registration and extracted shared read/write/seek helpers so sync and async paths cannot drift.
- Red-first async contracts in tests/hle/kernel_tests.cpp: open/read/lseek/close staging, poll, getAsyncStat, waitCB, busy, failed open, no-async, closed descriptor, invalid whence.

name: Research first — T17a
description:
Discover how the reference projects raise the frame rate, then record the decision before any code.

## Additional PSP references (2026-11-01)

Source: two PSP static recompilations that implement 60 fps by rendering
in-between frames over a locked 30 Hz logic tick. Behavioral reference only;
no code copied.

**highcmd/chinatown-wars-psp-recomp** (`runtime/src/ge_gl.cpp`, "frame
interpolation" block; `runtime/src/settings.h:7`; `ctw.ini.example`).
`fps = 30` keeps the game's rate; `fps = 60` adds in-between frames and
explicitly leaves the logic at 30. With interpolation on, draws are
*recorded* instead of executed. At GE FINISH the frame is executed twice:
first with every vertex at the midpoint between this draw and its matched
draw from the previous frame (the result kept per render target as
`midTex`), then normally. Matching key: texture reference, framebuffer
stride, vertex count and clear flag — deliberately **not** the framebuffer
address, because the game alternates two display buffers and an
address-based key matched nothing. A candidate partner whose vertices moved
implausibly far (average screen-space delta > 0.5) is rejected, which is the
camera-cut guard. Presentation order: the in-between picture at the first
vblank after the flip, the real frame at the next. Draws that never see a
FINISH are capped (200k) so a frame cannot grow without bound, and a match
percentage is logged for debugging.

**BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp** (`PLAN.md`, 2026-09-28 and
2026-10-11/10-13 entries). Also a locked 30 Hz logic, interpolated at
presentation. Instead of lerping vertices it reports every 3D draw (model
-> clip matrix, camera proj*view, viewport, match key of vtype/prim/count/
texture/framebuffer format+width/occurrence) and at `sceDisplaySetFrameBuf`
replays the frame into per-target shadow images with a per-draw
reprojection `R = lerp(M_prev, M_cur, 0.5) * inverse(M_cur)` in the vertex
shader. Unmatched main-camera draws get a camera-only R; a screen-space jump
over 0.3 screen widths counts as a cut and is not interpolated; only frames
finished exactly two vblanks apart are interpolated. The recording is
invalidated by texture eviction, target destruction, vertex-ring wrap and
GPU block transfers. Cost is one vblank of added latency. Shadows must be
seeded right before the frame first draws into a target, not from the
finished image, or effects that blend the previous frame are applied twice
(the reported "ghosting"); framebuffer double-buffering also broke the
initial match key. Per-vertex skinning interpolation was added later so
limbs are not stuck at 30.

**Implication.** Both PSP recompilations choose renderer interpolation over
raising the logic rate, which should demote option 3 (per-tick constant
patching) to last resort and make option 2 the likely target for T17a. Our
`ge::Draw` already carries final screen-space vertices (`runtime/ge/vertex.hpp:90`:
x, y, z, inv_w), so the Chinatown Wars vertex-midpoint method maps onto our
pipeline directly; matrix reprojection is the fallback if lerped vertices
look wrong for skinned/animated content. Required details to carry over:
a match key excluding alternating framebuffer addresses, a movement-outlier
cut guard, one vblank of latency, and invalidation on derived-state
rebuilds (which we already do on snapshot load).
result:
Research complete; no code written. Question: how do reference projects
raise the frame rate?

**RT64 (N64 renderer used by Zelda64Recomp).** Two renderers: one draws at
the game's native rate and synchronises back immediately so the game reads
correct RAM; the second replays the recorded draw calls at a higher
resolution and rate. Interpolation matches draw calls between frames by
rendering parameters, textures, position, orientation and tracked
velocities, decomposes transforms into translation/rotation/scale/skew,
interpolates the components separately and recomposes them, and also
interpolates texture scroll and per-vertex data when velocities exist. The
extended command set exists because some effects (depth-tested glows) break
at high frame rates or wide aspects.
Refs: rt64/rt64 README ("Frame interpolation", "Extended command set",
multi-renderer design).

**Zelda64Recomp.** Exposes the RT64 path (60 fps and above, widescreen) with
patch-level fixes such as the culling change so glows survive widescreen;
the game logic itself is untouched. Note this is a decompilation, so it can
also ship logic fixes that a static recomp cannot. Behavioral only.
Refs: Zelda64Recomp README, `patches/culling.c`.

**PPSSPP.** Does not raise a game's logic rate: it offers frame skip/auto
frame skip and vsync handling, and its display code compensates the 59.94
NTSC rate (1.001f in `Core/HLE/sceDisplay.cpp`). PSP 60 fps mods are cheat
codes that change the vblank wait count and the game's per-tick constants
through the CWCheat engine (`Core/CwCheat.cpp`, jokers/line-skip) — the
per-title patch shape of option 3.
Refs: hrydgard/ppsspp `Core/HLE/sceDisplay.cpp`, `Core/CwCheat.cpp`.

**Local.** Cadence is observable in our runtime:
`sceDisplayWaitVblankStartMulti` takes a vblank count
(`runtime/hle/hle_media.cpp:256`), `kVBlankPeriodUs` is 16'683
(`runtime/hle/kernel.hpp:95`), and `sceDisplaySetFrameBuf` counts flips
(`hle_media.cpp:216-233`). `ge::Draw` (`runtime/ge/state_machine.hpp:49`)
holds primitive, screen-space vertices, indices and state — no transform,
texture identity or velocity — so RT64-style matching needs a richer
per-draw record first. The one device run we have shows ~1 flip per 3.5
vblanks, so assuming 30 fps would be wrong.

Decision: measure first, then choose between pacing-only (default, always
on), renderer interpolation (host-only, largest effort) and a per-title
logic-rate override. No third-party code is copied (AGENTS #0).

name: T8c — Texture dump mode with hash-keyed PNG export
description:
Depends on: T8a.

Add dump mode to the runtime texture path: every decoded texture is written
to user storage as a PNG plus a textures.ini manifest (PPSSPP semantics as a
behavioral reference: stable content key, dimensions, format). The key must
cover geometry, pixel format, swizzle/bufw, texel bytes and all CLUT bytes so
a palette change produces a new key. Dumps go under a configured user
directory; nothing game-derived is committed.

PNG I/O must use an existing codec, never a hand-written one (AGENTS.md hard
limit 0): prefer system libpng with a version check, or a pinned MIT/public-
domain library recorded through the dependency/provenance process. Record the
choice in the T8 result and docs.

Tests (red first, synthetic TPL fixture):
- TC-8.2 dump half: dump to a temp dir, re-decode the PNG, pixels match the
  in-memory decode exactly.
- Two runs produce identical keys and bytes; changing one CLUT entry changes
  the key; a repeat dump does not overwrite a user replacement (T8d).

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code
"<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete
implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"`
for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "textures.ini" --extension cpp`; `gh search
code "texture dumping" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "texture
replacement hash"`; `gh search code "texture_collection" --extension cpp`.

Refs: psprecore `texture_collection.cpp`/`texture_replacement.cpp` (MIT,
behavioral reference only), PPSSPP texture replacement docs (semantics), T7
texture cache key tests. Gotchas: §7A.2 (no game content), §7B.3, §7F.3.
result:
Added runtime/tex/{png.hpp,png.cpp,dump.hpp,dump.cpp} and the gungnir_tex_png/gungnir_tex_dump targets, built when system libpng is available (1.6.59 on the host; zlib/libpng license, not vendored). read_png normalises RGB/RGBA/gray/palette/16-bit PNGs to RGBA8; write_png emits deterministic RGBA8 PNGs.

Dump mode hashes a content key (FNV-1a v1 over pixel format, swizzle, width, height, buffer width, CLUT format/mask, palette count/format, texel bytes and CLUT bytes) excluding live GE sampler state, so replacement lookups remain stable when clamp/filter changes. It writes new/<KEY>.png and appends textures.ini entries ([options] version=1 hash=gungnir64, [hashes] KEY = new/KEY.png) without duplicating keys (case-normalised). Existing PNGs are compared pixel-for-pixel: identical files are skipped, different files fail key_collision, corrupt files fail existing_png_invalid, so dump never overwrites user data. Batch dumps handle multiple textures; duplicate same-content keys are collapsed, different content under one key fails key_collision.

Tests in tests/tex/dump_tests.cpp: key stability and sensitivity to CLUT/texel/buffer-width/swizzle/format, live-sampler independence, PNG round-trip, manifest creation/de-duplication, batch dumps, CLUT-change dumps, collision/corrupt rejection and named invalid inputs. Mutation: removing palette bytes from the key fails 'CLUT bytes change the key'. Local dump check on six user containers wrote 14 textures and re-read every PNG. Full suite 77/77 green; repository_check PASS (223 files).

References used: PPSSPP PR #8715, the texture-replacement wiki and GPU/Common/TextureReplacer.cpp for [options]/[hashes]/[hashranges]/mipmap/empty-filename semantics (behavior only; no code adopted), psprecore runtime/src/gpu/texture_collection.cpp (MIT) for the content-hash + PNG + index dump shape, LiinkPK/Texture-Replacement-Tool-for-PPSSPP for replacement-pack workflow (binary-only, no source adopted), and libpng for the codec. Docs: docs/TEXTURE_REPLACEMENT.md records the layout and the explicit non-compatibility with PPSSPP's 24-hex key.

# T14a — Manual QA campaign

**Depends on:** T13b, T13c, T13d, T13e.

**Goal.** Every matrix cell has a dated, signed report; the documented from-scratch pipeline reaches the title screen and menu on the adb device; every finding is fixed red-first or tracked.

**Work.**
- Write `docs/QA.md`: the standard script plus the Gungnir-specific script (title → menu → first gameplay transition). Cover cold boot, touch menu, gamepad menu (paired + built-in handheld), overlay hide-on-pad, suspend/resume rendering recovery, rotation ignored, save/load, touch haptic tick, rumble status (from T11: touch-control haptics landed there; game/battle rumble is still unknown), audio smoke, 30-minute soak, and thermal/battery observations. Include the evidence/sign-off template and the three-cold-boot rule.
- Run the matrix: x86_64 emulator (SwiftShader) plus at least one physical Adreno arm64 phone and one non-Adreno/handheld where available. Ask the user for device access and interaction; use adb and `scripts/android/*`, never xdotool.

- Run three consecutive cold boots per device. Run suspend/resume cycles and a 30-minute soak on at least one physical device; record crash/thermal/audio counters and a recording hash, not frames.
- Fix findings red-first wherever host-testable (reproducing test before the fix); file device-only defects as tracked dex tasks and link them from the report. Every finding ends with a regression test or an open defect ID.
- Include the Android memstick save/load path and the audio smoke in at least one cell; record named gaps rather than passing them silently.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- A QA-report structure test (`tests/test_qa_reports.py`) validates required fields, matrix cells, date/build SHA, and pass/fail counts; it fails before the first report exists.
- Any host-testable finding gets a red reproduction in the owning suite before its fix.
- Re-run the three cold boots after every fix; a regression re-opens the cell.

**Acceptance / evidence.** TC-13.1, TC-14.2 and TC-14.3 pass with dated reports; every matrix cell is signed; no game frames or hashes of game content are committed; every finding has a red test or a tracked open defect.

**Guardrails.** "CI is green" is not device evidence; one successful boot is not evidence. Do not fabricate a device result — record what was actually run. No xdotool; ask the user for GUI interaction when needed. PPSSPP is an oracle only.

**Docs.** `docs/QA.md`, `docs/qa/<date>-<device>.md`, `docs/BRINGUP.md`, `docs/PROGRESS.md` notes.

name: T18a — Implement crisp text: sampling, HD atlas and replacement wiring
description:
Implement crisp text in the order parent T18 defines. Each step is useful on
its own and must be independently verifiable on device.

1. Measure (blocking, before choosing): dump the text atlases and record
   keys, format, cell geometry and palette alpha levels; log the sampler
   state and the on-screen scale of text draws. Add the numbers to
   `docs/TEXTURE_REPLACEMENT.md` or a new `docs/TEXT.md`. Never infer the
   atlas from screenshots.
2. Wire `runtime/tex/replace.cpp` into the GE draw path (no call site uses
   it today), keyed by the T8c content key, native texture on any error.
3. Per-texture sampling override for text atlases (nearest/linear), behind
   config; off must be pixel-identical to today.
4. HD atlas generator: extend `tools/textures/repack_font_atlas.py` (or add
   a sibling) to accept per-glyph anti-aliased coverage fitted to each
   glyph's original ink box, emitting an RGBA atlas at Nx with the same
   cell grid. Keep nearest replication as the no-invention option. Reject a
   glyph whose ink box differs from the original unless explicitly allowed
   (layout guard).
5. Only if 3-4 are not enough: SDF/MSDF atlas plus a shader variant, off by
   default, documented as an extra path.
6. Docs: how to generate a pack from one's own dump, the ink-box rule, and
   that nothing is shipped.

Red-first tests:
- UV/layout: a 4x replacement atlas samples to the same glyph in the same
  cell; a synthetic text run keeps identical quad positions and advances.
- Ink box: an upscaled glyph with a different ink box is rejected with a
  named error (layout guard).
- Sampling: forcing nearest for one text key changes only that texture;
  off is byte-identical.
- Failure: unknown key, corrupt PNG, wrong cell grid, non-uniform scale —
  named errors and the native texture stays.
- Mutation: drop the normalized-UV mapping (use texel coordinates) and
  confirm the layout test fails for that reason.

Acceptance: on-device before/after screenshots of dialogue and menus at
native scale, no reflow; no new stall under the frame watchdog;
`repository_check` PASS; full suite green; QA evidence under gitignored
`build/qa/`.

Reference discovery (all tasks): `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add
`--extension cpp` for C/C++), then `gh search issues`; record new
references. Preferred references: hrydgard/ppsspp `TextureScalerCommon` and
`TextureReplacer`, BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp texture packs, and
`Chlumsky/msdfgen` if SDF is chosen. Record which mechanism was reused or
rejected.

Red-first rule applies (plan section 8.1).

name: Single-copy dedup retention (drop entry.data duplicate)

name: Research first — T18a
description: Discover how the references raise text quality and what our font atlas allows, then record the decision before any code.
result:
Research complete; no code written. Question: how can the text be made
crisp at phone resolution?

**Where the roughness comes from.** Three separate losses: the source is a
13-pixel bitmap, the frame is magnified ~2.7x (480x272 logical on a 1080p
phone), and filtering is either linear (blur) or nearest (blocky) at a
non-integer scale. Rendering at a higher internal resolution fixes geometry,
not the atlas; the same is true of Chinatown Wars (`render_scale` + `filter`
only) and The 3rd Birthday (texture packs, not render scale).

**Reference implementations.**
- PPSSPP: texture *scaling* at load — `GPU/Common/TextureScalerCommon.h`
  exposes XBRZ, HYBRID, BICUBIC and HYBRID_BICUBIC, with an optional
  deposterize pass, driven by the texture-scaling settings. Texture
  *replacement* packs are supported at any resolution, with per-entry
  `[filtering] nearest|linear` in `textures.ini`
  (`GPU/Common/TextureReplacer.cpp`). Hashes are content+size and
  replacements at a different size work because UVs are normalized
  (`ReplacedTexture::Prepare` divides by `newW/newH` for ranges).
- BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp: texture packs at any resolution ("4x
  for an HD pack", `mods/README.md`), PPSSPP pack compatibility
  (`runtime/src/rt/texpack_ppsspp.c`); it parses PGF for system-font text
  (`runtime/src/rt/pgf.c`), which Gungnir does not need.
- highcmd/chinatown-wars-psp-recomp: no texture upscaling; per-texture
  filter choice and `hud_scale` only. Evidence that resolution alone leaves
  text soft.
- RT64/Zelda64Recomp: HD texture replacement; texcoord scaling is only
  needed for framebuffer-tile addressing, not normalized-UV sprites.
- SDF text: Valve, "Improved Alpha-Tested Magnification for Vector Textures
  and Special Effects" (SIGGRAPH 2007); `Chlumsky/msdfgen` (MIT) generates
  SDF/MSDF atlases from vector shapes. Needs a vector source and a shader
  variant.

**Constraint that shapes the answer.** Horizontal layout comes from each
glyph's ink width (T8e). A replacement glyph with a different ink box
reflows text: centred lines drift and dialogue boxes overflow. Safe options
are therefore (a) scale the existing ink (nearest/xBRZ) or (b) fit a
re-rasterized glyph into the original ink box. Free re-typesetting is not
safe without also changing the game's layout.

**Options.**
A. Sampling policy: force nearest for text/CLUT atlases. Cheap, removes
   linear blur; blocky at fractional scale and can shimmer.
B. Atlas upscale at load: nearest (no invention) or xBRZ/MMPX/deposterize
   (smoother, invented edges), cached by content key, derived only.
C. HD atlas via the replacement path: RGBA at Nx, same cell grid and ink
   boxes; either nearest replication (existing repack tool) or anti-aliased
   glyphs from a user-supplied font fitted to each ink box. Best
   quality/effort if replacements reach the draw path.
D. SDF/MSDF atlas plus a shader variant: best at any scale; needs a vector
   source (13px bitmaps are a poor source) and a new shader path.
E. Host-side text re-rendering: decode the glyph quads and draw native text;
   highest quality and the only option that can change size, but needs the
   game's text path, metrics and layout. Last resort.

**Gap found.** `runtime/tex/replace.cpp` (T8d) is a loader only: no
renderer or GE call site uses `TextureReplacements` today. Any HD-atlas
path starts by wiring it into the draw path, keyed by the T8c content key,
with the native texture as the fail-closed fallback.

**Legal.** No game font, glyph bitmap or texture may be committed; an HD
atlas is generated locally from the user's dump and a user-supplied source.
The repack tool's byte-identical identity gate stays (AGENTS 1-2).

**Measurement still needed before choosing.** Dump the text atlases and
record keys, cell geometry and palette alpha levels; log the sampler state
and on-screen scale of text draws. A palette with only binary alpha cannot
carry anti-aliasing, which decides between C (RGBA replacement) and a
palette-preserving TPL repack.

name: T18 — Text legibility: crisp font rendering at phone resolution
description:
Make the game's text crisp at phone resolution. Text is the roughest part of
the picture today: a 13-pixel bitmap atlas magnified ~2.7x on a 1080p phone.

Scope decision: this targets sharpness at the current layout. Making text
larger is a layout change (line breaks, boxes, centring) and is not in this
task; PPSSPP and Chinatown Wars both scale HUD elements without reflowing
dialog text, so size is a separate feature.

Facts (verified in this repo):
- The dialog font is a 4bpp PSP-swizzled TPL with a 16-entry RGBA8888
  palette, 13x13 / 16x14 cells (T8e,
  `tools/textures/repack_font_atlas.py`).
- The game has no width table: the advance is the glyph ink width, so any
  glyph replacement that changes its ink box reflows text.
- Text is GE quads sampling the atlas. Textures are uploaded at native size,
  there are no mipmaps, and filtering is the GE bit
  (`runtime/ge/state_machine.cpp:339`).
- The game imports no sceFont/PGF; there is no system-font path to improve.
- `runtime/tex/replace.cpp` implements the content-keyed replacement loader
  (T8d) but no GE draw/renderer call site uses it yet.

Options ranked (detail in `Research first — T18a`):
A. Per-texture sampling policy (nearest for text atlases), measured first.
B. Atlas upscale at load (nearest / xBRZ / MMPX / deposterize), cached by
   content key.
C. HD atlas through the existing replacement path: RGBA, any resolution,
   same cell grid and ink boxes; glyphs from a user-supplied source fitted
   to each ink box. Preferred if replacements are wired into the draw path.
D. SDF/MSDF atlas plus a shader variant (best magnification, most work).
E. Host-side text re-rendering (last resort; needs the game's text path).

Legal: no game font, glyph bitmap or texture is committed. An HD atlas is
generated locally from the user's own dump and a user-supplied source; the
existing repack tool's identity gate stays (AGENTS hard limits 1-2).

Decomposition (dex): T18a is the implementation, with its research step
`Research first — T18a`. Split further only if it grows past one reviewable
change.

Status 2026-11-01: research complete; implementation not started.

name: GE TEXSCALE/TEXOFFSET
description: Apply TEXSCALEU/V (0x48/0x49) and TEXOFFSETU/V (0x4A/0x4B) to UVs (perspective-correct path). Scope: decode into texture state, software sampler + Vulkan UV transform, parity test. References (behavioral only): BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp runtime/src/rt/ge.c (TEXSCALE/TEXOFFSET perspective-correct UV); highcmd/chinatown-wars-psp-recomp runtime/src/ge_render.cpp pipe for equivalents. Red-first: scaled-UV fixture fails before, passes after. Evidence: world quads sample the right texel windows. Findings 2026-11-02: vertex-stage TEXSCALE/OFFSET was already correct (event frame: 781 transform draws use sc=(2.00031,4.5) off=(-0.0006,-5); software math equivalent to references; UVs in frame JSON confirm application). Actual defect found: Vulkan wrap mode inverted (clamp_u/v fed to repeat-semantics sampler params) so repeat draws clamped to edges on device/headless Vulkan. Fix renames wrap_u/v to clamp_u/v and corrects address modes, verified by a repeat-wrap parity case. Regression check: software re-render byte-identical, device event scene identical layout (dark fade masks texture detail), PPSSPP side-by-side in /tmp/opencode/scene/vs-ppsspp-wrap.png shows only the known fade delta.
result: Done and committed as bc9127c. Vertex-stage TEXSCALE/OFFSET verified already correct (781 transform draws use sc=(2.00031,4.5) off=(-0.0006,-5); software math equivalent to both references; frame JSON shows scaled UVs). Actual defect: Vulkan wrap inverted (clamp flags into repeat-semantics sampler params). Renamed wrap_u/v to clamp_u/v across DrawState/VulkanDrawState/sampler/Android bridge; corrected address modes. Red-first: repeat-wrap parity with 0..2 UVs (observed red), texwrap_decode contract (observed red via temporary neutering). Full suite green, repository_check PASS. Regression: host software re-render byte-identical; device event scene identical layout (dark fade masks texture detail); PPSSPP side-by-side vs-ppsspp-wrap.png shows only known fade delta. Note: frame capture varies run to run on this animated scene (799/1784/2046 draws); comparisons use same-count pairs plus render bytes.

name: Research first — T16a
description:
Discover how the reference projects widen the view, then record the decision before any code.

## Additional PSP references (2026-11-01)

Source: two static-recompilation projects of PSP titles. Behavioral reference
only; no code copied.

**BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp** (PSP static recomp, Vulkan GE runtime).
Its widescreen implementation is per-title and guest-side, not a generic
post-projection scale: function-entry hooks give the game's own cameras the
window aspect — `cam_projection 0x08BBB194` and `cam_setup 0x08B435B8`
("give the game's cameras the window aspect so it renders and culls wider
itself"). Consequences it documents: flat 2D/ortho HUD is squeezed into a
centred 16:9 area, genuinely full-screen draws stretch, HUD draws parked
off-screen are skipped, and squeezed HUD draws are clipped to the PSP
screen area with the scissor. A small (<=16 vertices) perspective quad on
an unwidened camera that spans the PSP screen width is treated as a 2D
full-screen effect and stretched; the same rule fixed the dark edge strips
in one scene. The aspect mode is in the in-game menu, and `mods/` ships a
disabled FOV example (`fov.c`, `mod.toml`) that patches `$f12` of
`cam_setup`, with the aspect in `$f13`.
Refs: `PLAN.md` entries 2026-10-23 ("Do all the missing stuff", part 1 and
the tunnel-strip fix), `mods/example_wider_fov/fov.c`, `mods/example_wider_fov/mod.toml`.

**highcmd/chinatown-wars-psp-recomp** (PSP static recomp, OpenGL GE
runtime). It does not widen the FOV. Fullscreen keeps the 480:272 frame
fitted and letterboxed (`docs/OPTIONS.md`), `render_scale` renders at
480*N x 272*N rather than stretching, and the HUD is handled separately with
`hud_scale` (100/75/50: elements shrink towards their corner or edge;
full-screen menus keep their size). Fullscreen is borderless at the desktop
mode or exclusive at `resolution @ refresh`.
Refs: `docs/OPTIONS.md`, `ctw.ini.example`, `runtime/src/settings.h`.

**Implication.** The camera-argument hook is a third design option for T16a:
the game computes the wider projection and culling itself, which behaves
better than a host-side post-projection scale but needs per-title RE
(addresses, calling convention, camera objects). The 3rd Birthday's
heuristics (full-screen quad, small-quad-on-unwidened-camera, scissored HUD)
are directly reusable for the per-draw classification and the per-title
override, and Chinatown Wars' `hud_scale` is the reference for shrinking HUD
elements instead of stretching them.
result:
Research complete; no code written. Question: how do the reference projects
widen the view?

**RT64 / Zelda64Recomp (N64 recomp + renderer).** Aspect handling lives in
the renderer: the projection is widened to any aspect ratio, the HUD can be
pinned to 16:9 in ultrawide, and 2D/pixel-space effects are fixed per
effect through the extended GBI (`gEXVertexZTest`) plus patch-level culling
changes (`patches/culling.c`: enable the glow while the projected Z position
is valid). The README documents animation quirks at the edges of very wide
ratios. Behavioral only; no code copied.
Refs: rt64/rt64 README (extended command set, widescreen integration);
Zelda64Recomp README "Widescreen and Ultrawide Support" and
`patches/culling.c`.

**DuckStation (PS1).** One `WidescreenHack` setting
(`src/core/settings.cpp`), with per-game metadata able to force it off when
a game already ships a widescreen patch (`src/core/cheats.cpp`:
`disable_widescreen_rendering`), and the auto/forced aspect choice handled
at presentation (`src/core/imgui_overlays.cpp`). The hack widens the 3D
projection and leaves 2D at native width — the same 3D-only contract
proposed here.
Refs: stenzek/duckstation `src/core/settings.cpp`, `src/core/cheats.cpp`,
`src/core/imgui_overlays.cpp`.

**PPSSPP (PSP).** Deliberately has no generic view widening: the
display-layout code only fits/stretches the 480x272 image
(`GPU/Common/PresentationCommon.cpp`: aspect ratio, crop-to-16x9, integer
scaling). Real PSP widescreen is a per-frame CWCheat code that rewrites the
game's projection constants (`Core/CwCheat.cpp`: joker and line-skip
opcodes). That is the state of the art on the platform and the reason a
per-title override belongs in the design.
Refs: hrydgard/ppsspp `GPU/Common/PresentationCommon.cpp`,
`Core/CwCheat.cpp`.

**Local anchor.** `runtime/ge/vertex.cpp` builds `world_view_projection_`
(line 257) and applies the GE viewport (line 412) in our own code;
`runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp:174` fits the 480x272 frame into the
surface. Unlike PPSSPP the widening needs no guest memory patch; unlike
DuckStation, 2D is not a separate command stream, so draws need
classification (perspective vs ortho/screen-space) and overrides.

Decision: host-side projection widening + presentation fill, per-draw 2D
exclusion, per-title override, FMV pillarboxed, mode recorded in the
snapshot config identity. No third-party code is copied (AGENTS #0); the
references above are behavioral only.

name: Gungnir Recomp — Master Plan
description:
(Complete plan lives at .dex/plan.md in this repo; §3 reference-projects table is omitted below only for size — see the file. Subtasks T1–T13 each carry their plan section.)

# Gungnir Recomp — Master Plan

**Target:** Gungnir (USA) — *Gungnir: Inferno of the Demon Lance and the War of Heroes*, ULUS-10592
**Goal:** Static recompilation of the game's Allegrex code to native C++, running on Android — from the user's own `game.chd` to a boot on an adb-connected device.
**First milestone (locked):** title screen rendered on device + menu input navigable (touch + gamepad).
**Plan date:** 2026-10-30. Source: 14-project discovery survey (see §3).

---

## 0. Hard constraints (non-negotiable)

1. **No proprietary content, code, or work is ever committed.** No game ISO/CHD/ELF/PRX, no decrypted modules, no game assets (DAR contents, TPL textures, VAG audio, script `.bin`), no game text (original or translated), no game screenshots, no Sony firmware, no PGF fonts, no KIRK/DRM keys, no Adreno driver binaries, no generated recompilation output (which is a derivative of the copyrighted executable).
2. The repo contains only: original tooling and runtime we author, third-party code with licenses preserved and attributed, synthetic fixtures of our own authorship, documentation, and scripts that operate on **user-supplied local files**.
3. Decryption of `~PSP` modules runs **out-of-process** using user-supplied tools (pspdecrypt / PPSSPP devtools). We ship no decryption implementation and no keys. Same for Adreno driver `.zip`s: user-supplied, extracted to app-private storage, never bundled or committed.
4. Enforcement is structural, not aspirational: `.gitignore` with rationale, `tools/repository_check.py` (extension + magic-byte + blob-size + ignore-rule audit) in CI, secret scanning, and fail-closed CI (`exit 77` skips) for tests that need private game input.
5. Game-derived facts that are acceptable to publish: disc identity (size 262,766,592 B, CRC32 `183F3EDC`, redump-recorded), format field layouts, NID values, guest addresses and record sizes (RE facts). Binaries, hashes of binaries pinned as "the expected dump", and content derived from them stay local.
6. **No clean-room reimplementations.** If work reduces to implementing a format, codec, or protocol that existing tools or libraries already implement, **stop and ask before writing anything**: use the existing tool out-of-process, or adopt an audited open-source implementation with provenance. Clean-room reimplementation is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md hard limit #0).

## 1. Decisions locked (2026-10-30)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Foundation | Adopt an **MIT-licensed PSPRecomp-framework core** (jessicanataliagta/PSPRecomp lineage; TeamGDB/Yakumo framework subset is the same lineage, more mature). We write: Gungnir profile, Android shell, Vulkan renderer, driver loader, texture/shader systems. |
| Project license | **GPL-3.0-or-later** (max reuse freedom: MIT + BSD + LGPL-dynamic + GPL-2.0-or-later + GPL-3.0 sources; rejects CC BY-NC-SA and unattributed code) |
| Android baseline | **minSdk 26, Vulkan 1.1 required**, AAudio available; ABIs `arm64-v8a` + `x86_64` (emulator) |
| Renderer | **Vulkan-only** (no GL ES fallback); software rasterizer kept as parity oracle; post-processing chain (upscale + LCD/scanline shaders) after GE compositing |
| Audio | AAudio (Android) / SDL audio (desktop); ATRAC3(+) via LGPL `at3_standalone`-class decoder with notices |
| Game data on device | SAF document-tree picker **or** `adb push` to `getExternalFilesDir()`. **No** `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` |
| Adreno drivers | User-supplied `.zip` ICDs (Mesa Turnip / Qualcomm-style) loaded via custom Vulkan loader; per-driver selection; fail-closed fallback to system driver |
| Input | Touch overlay (editable layout) + SDL3 gamepad with per-device profiles (Ayn/Ayaneo-class handhelds) + keyboard/mouse (desktop dev); rumble/haptics via SDL gamepad rumble + Android Vibrator fallback |
| Textures | Hash-keyed dump→replace pipeline (PPSSPP `textures.ini` semantics) + high-res font-atlas re-rasterization for dialog text (Gungnir stores text in TPL atlases and baked into TPL images) |
| Disc input | **Intake accepts ISO only.** `game.chd` is converted once, user-side — e.g. [CHDStudio](https://github.com/purelogiccode/CHDStudio) (GUI, recommended) or `chdman extractcd` (MAME CLI). Our pipeline never parses CHD. Converter correctness is *verified, not trusted* — the identity gate (size + CRC32) validates whatever produced the ISO. |
| Code reuse | **Adopt, don't reimplement.** Clean-room implementations of existing formats/codecs/protocols are **not sanctioned** without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0): use existing tools out-of-process (CHDStudio/chdman) or adopt audited open-source code with provenance (Yakumo MIT subset → `third_party/yakumo/`). Applies to everything upcoming too (e.g. PGF parsing, ATRAC3, image codecs, JSON) — check the reference projects and library landscape first, always. |
| Testing | **Red-first (TDD where relevant):** the failing test lands before the implementation, and is confirmed red for the expected reason. Regression fixes start from a failing reproduction. No task closes with untested behavior. |
| Device validation | **Mandatory manual QA on an adb device** before any milestone touching device behavior can close — structured, recorded QA (build ID, device, steps, expected/actual, sign-off), never "CI is green" alone |

## 2. Target facts — Gungnir (USA)

Facts from the discovery survey (kreycai/gungnir-ptbr format docs, redump, PPSSPP logs). These shape the whole plan:

- **Disc:** UMD ISO 9660, 262,766,592 B, CRC32 `183F3EDC` (redump 29734). The local `game.chd` is an LZMA CHD of this disc (header verified: `MComprHD` v5, `lzma`). JP is ULJM-05779 (v1.01) — different offsets everywhere; this plan targets **USA only**.
- **`PSP_GAME/SYSDIR/EBOOT.BIN`:** 3,336,096 B at ISO offset `0x110000`, `~PSP`-encrypted (magic `0x5053507E`); `BOOT.BIN` sibling is the plaintext form on some discs. Decrypted form: PRX ELF `e_type 0xFFA0`, segment 0 at file offset `0xC0` with `vaddr = file_offset − 0xC0`, relocation section type `0x70000020` (entries 8 B: `r_offset:u32, r_info:u32`, types **2 = R_MIPS_32, 5 = HI16, 6 = LO16**). ~3,552 strings live in the EBOOT (vaddr `0x19F000–0x1D8000` region).
- **USRDIR archives (DAR format):** `ini.dar` (61 files incl. font atlases `font11pt.tpl`/`font12pt.tpl`), `voice.dar` (voice audio), `data.dar` (~44 MB, plaintext, 1,295 `.tpl` textures + ~13,998 strings + script `.bin`s), plus `INSDIR/DATA.DAR`. DAR header = 4×u32 LE `[nfiles, data_start, names_off, table_off]`; entries = 16 B `[name_off, stored_size, decomp_size, data_off]`; zlib per entry when `decomp_size > stored_size`; **`stored_size == 0` means stored uncompressed** (real size in `decomp_size`).
- **Text:** fullwidth Shift-JIS (cp932), NUL-terminated; engine break commands `5C 6E` in DAR data, `0x3B` in EBOOT. Script `.bin` files (`event/`, `map/`, `worldmap/`, `setup*/`) = `[u32 type, u32 n, u32 table_off=12]` + n absolute u32 offsets + bytecode with absolute-address jumps — **files must not change size** or every pointer/jump must be remapped.
- **Fonts/textures:** TPL containers (0x30 B header; per-texture `H,W,BW,bpp,data_off`), 4bpp PSP-swizzled (16×8 blocks), index-as-alpha, and 8bpp+CLUT. Dialog glyph advance = ink width (width table). UI text is also **baked into images** (actname/tutorial/location pages) — text upscaling has two fronts: font atlas re-rasterization + image texture replacement.
- **Engine/runtime expectations (PPSSPP logs):** calls `sceKernelLoadModule` (PRX overlay tiers needed), "render to area containing texture" (feedback path in GE), one audio-decode quirk. PPSSPP rates it Perfect→Playable — our behavioral oracle.
- **DAR size fields in ISO 9660 directory records are both-endian** (LE + BE 4 bytes later) — any repack must patch both (we don't repack the ISO for recomp, but the asset pipeline touches DARs inside `build/`).

## 4. Architecture & repo layout

```
gungnir-recomp/
├── AGENTS.md                    # single policy authority (hard limits, evidence rules)
├── LICENSE                      # GPL-3.0-or-later
├── .recomp.json                 # recomp.fyi card
├── .gitignore                   # game data / keys / generated code, each with rationale
├── dependencies.json            # pinned third-party revisions (azazel6 pattern)
├── CMakeLists.txt               # desktop + Android shared build (nk_add_title_runtime shape)
├── cmake/Deps.cmake             # fetch-or-reuse with lock+digest
├── configs/nids.csv             # NID registry (BSD pspsdk headers / fetch-with-checksum)
├── tools/
│   ├── repository_check.py      # IP gate (azazel6 adaptation) — CI, pre-push
│   ├── package_notices.py       # generated THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt from one JSON
│   ├── intake/                  # chd→iso→extract→decrypt-hook→manifest
│   ├── analyze, codegen         # analysis + AOT (adopted MIT core + our glue)
│   ├── dar.py, tpl.py           # DAR/TPL readers (user's local files only)
│   ├── textures/                # dump/replace + font-atlas repack
│   └── ghidra/ExportPSPFunctions.java   # optional function census
├── runtime/                     # guest memory, dispatch, interpreter, HLE, GE, post
│   ├── hle/  ge/  post/  input/  audio/  savedata/
│   └── platform/adreno/         # custom Vulkan ICD loader
├── profiles/gungnir/
│   ├── config.toml              # facts-vs-choices (wizardengineer split)
│   └── local/                   # GITIGNORED: hashes, address pins, per-dump data
├── android/                     # Gradle (Kotlin DSL) + JNI shell
├── assets/shaders/{ge,post}/    # committed GLSL (ours), SPIR-V embedded at build
├── assets/input_profiles/       # handheld gamepad profiles (ours)
├── tests/fixtures/              # synthetic Allegrex fixtures of OUR authorship
├── data/milestones.json         # hst-decomp ratchet ledger
├── docs/                        # see §6 documentation checkpoints
└── build/                       # GITIGNORED: game tree, generated code, outputs
```

**Pipeline:** `game.chd` → [T3 intake] → `build/game/` (verified ISO, decrypted ELF, manifest) → [T5 analyze+codegen] → `build/generated/` (chunked C++ TUs) → [T6/T7 runtime] → Linux desktop boot → [T9/T10/T11 Android] → adb device → [T13] title screen.

## 5. Tasks

Each task: dependencies, work, deliverables, test cases (TC), docs checkpoint, reference callouts, gotchas (pointer to §7 register).

**Red-first rule for all tasks (§8.1):** each TC is written and observed red *before* the implementation that satisfies it; bug fixes begin with a reproducing red test; no task below closes with a red or disabled TC. Tasks touching runtime semantics also carry a mutation check.

### T1 — Scaffolding + IP guardrails
**Depends on:** — (first task)
**Work:** git init (keep `game.chd` untracked forever); `LICENSE`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore` (case-insensitive blocks for `*.iso *.chd *.cso *.elf *.prx *.pbp *.bin *.pmf *.at3 *.vag`, `keys/`, `generated/`, `game/`, `PSP_GAME/`, `build/`, `profiles/*/local/`, analysis dumps — with rationale comments, nakagawa style); `tools/repository_check.py` (magic-byte sniff of git index for ELF/`~PSP`/CHD/PE, >1 MB blob rejection, ignore-rule regression tests, secret scan); `docs/LEGAL.md` (the IP charter = §0); `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`; `.recomp.json`.
**Test cases:**
- TC-1.1 `repository_check.py` passes on clean tree.
- TC-1.2 Staging a dummy `.iso`/`.elf`/`~PSP` blob fails the check (each magic recognized).
- TC-1.3 Ignore-rule regression: creating `build/game/x.iso` never appears in `git status`.
- TC-1.4 `game.chd` in workdir is never matched by `git ls-files`.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/LEGAL.md` + `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md` + `AGENTS.md` written **before any code lands**.
**Refs:** nakagawa-recomp (`.gitignore`, AGENTS.md), azazel6 (`repository_check.py`), psprism (`LICENSING.md`), Yakumo (`SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`).
**Gotchas:** §7A.

### T2 — Third-party dependency ledger + license machine
**Depends on:** T1
**Work:** `dependencies.json` pinning: MIT PSPRecomp framework core (choose jessicanataliagta/PSPRecomp `include/+src/` or Yakumo framework subset — record exact commit + provenance), CHD reader (libchdr or chd-rs — audit first), SDL3 (pinned commit, nakagawa `deps.cmake` pattern), stb image, tiny-AES-class public-domain crypto (savedata later), NID name data (BSD pspsdk headers or `pspdev/psp-ghidra-scripts` fetch-with-checksum — **never** copy psprism's unattributed `ppsspp_niddb.xml`; PPSSPP-derived tables are usable under our GPL-3.0 **with attribution**); `cmake/Deps.cmake` (fetch-or-reuse, lock+digest, offline-capable); `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES/`; `tools/package_notices.py` → `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`.
**Test cases:**
- TC-2.1 Clean checkout + one command materializes all deps at verified commits (digest check fails on wrong revision).
- TC-2.2 `package_notices.py` output covers every vendored file (CI gate: no unlisted file under `third_party/`).
- TC-2.3 License gate rejects a deliberately added CC BY-NC-SA component.
**Findings (2026-10-30):** first pin landed early with T3: `dependencies.json` + `third_party/yakumo/PROVENANCE.md` + in-tree LICENSE (MIT, pin `b61852a`) — the template the remaining entries (SDL3, CHD reader if ever needed, stb, ATRAC decoder) must follow. **License-implication of §1 Code reuse:** clean-room reimplementations are not sanctioned — where no adoptable code exists for something we need, **stop and ask** (that decision belongs to the user, not the agent).
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/PROVENANCE.md` (per-subtree: upstream, commit, license, disposition).
**Refs:** azazel6 (`dependencies.json`), nakagawa (`deps.cmake` + notice generation), wizardengineer (`fetch-niddb.sh` + checksum), psprism (attribution gap as cautionary tale).
**Gotchas:** §7A.5–A.7.

### T3 — Game intake pipeline (`game.iso` → verified local build tree)
**Depends on:** T1
**Work:** `tools/intake/`: (1) **disc input = ISO only** (locked decision §1: `game.chd` is converted user-side via [CHDStudio](https://github.com/purelogiccode/CHDStudio) or `chdman extractcd`; intake refuses `.chd` with a named error pointing at `docs/INTAKE.md`; we never parse CHD — the identity gate *verifies, not trusts*, the converter); (2) identity gate: size 262,766,592 + CRC32 `183F3EDC`, **fail closed** on mismatch; (3) ISO9660 extract of `PSP_GAME/` tree (EBOOT.BIN, USRDIR `*.dar`, INSDIR, PARAM.SFO — verify disc ID ULUS-10592); (4) decrypt hook — **no decryption code in-repo**; invoke user-supplied pspdecrypt/PPSSPP "Dump decrypted EBOOT.BIN" out-of-process, accept `BOOT.BIN` plaintext or user-provided decrypted ELF, validate PRX shape (`e_type 0xFFA0`, `vaddr = file_offset − 0xC0`, reloc section `0x70000020`, types 2/5/6); (5) `build/game/manifest.json`: module list, SHA-256s, segments, reloc counts, NID import inventory. All outputs under `build/` (gitignored).
**Test cases:**
- TC-3.1 End-to-end on local `game.iso` produces manifest.json with expected module set. *(Covered by `tests/test_intake.py` — written and observed red before implementation.)*
- TC-3.2 Wrong-CRC input (bit-flipped ISO) aborts with named error `IDENTITY_MISMATCH`; `.chd` input aborts with named error `CHD_NOT_SUPPORTED` pointing at CHDStudio.
- TC-3.3 Truncated/decrypted-partially ELF rejected (magic + program-header checks): `~PSP` magic → `ENCRYPTED_EXECUTABLE` (points at out-of-process decrypt), truncated/garbage → `ELF_INVALID`.
- TC-3.4 Every intermediate artifact lands under `build/`; `repository_check` still green.
**Findings (2026-10-30, from implementation):** ISO9660 + ELF32 + PARAM.SFO parsing is **adopted** from TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, `third_party/yakumo/`, pin `b61852a`) — not clean-room, per §1 Code reuse. Intake shape is therefore a C++ reader tool (`tools/intake/intake_tool.cpp`, subcommands `iso-extract`/`elf-inspect`/`sfo-info`, built by root `CMakeLists.txt`) + Python orchestrator (`tools/intake/intake.py`: identity gate + manifest via stdlib `zlib`/`hashlib`/`json` — existing implementations). Known gap: vendored `elf32.cpp` handles reloc section `0x700000A0` only; Gungnir's EBOOT uses `0x70000020` — intake counts both via its own section walk (`ElfSection` list + raw entry scan), vendored code stays unpatched (recorded in `third_party/yakumo/PROVENANCE.md`). Manifest records the actual section type found, for T5.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/INTAKE.md` (user-facing: how to supply their own disc, external decrypt tools, what the gates check).
**Refs:** gungnir-ptbr (ISO offsets, `~PSP` layout — facts only), wtf-psp-recomp (`extract.ps1` report style), Yakumo (`prepare_game.sh` SHA-pin pattern), codepdbh (`--verify-only` identity gate).
**Gotchas:** §7B (format traps), §7A.1–A.3.

### T4 — Framework core integration + oracle harness (Linux desktop)
**Depends on:** T2
**Work:** Root CMake + `runtime/`: guest memory (32 MB RAM @ `0x08800000`, **16 KB scratchpad @ `0x00010000`**, VRAM @ `0x04000000`, cache-mirror collapse), full-coverage Allegrex decoder (incl. ADDI; tolerant data-as-code decode), AOT codegen to `build/generated/` chunked TUs (never committed; content-hash fingerprint staleness gate), dispatch with **interpreter fallback + FNV block cache as a permanent tier**, forward-branch yield counters. Test strategy: committed synthetic Allegrex fixtures (our authorship) run under interpreter AND AOT with trace equality; hand-computed self-tests (sal063 pattern — expectations never generated from the implementation); `ctest` on Linux x86_64.
**Test cases:**
- TC-4.1 All synthetic fixtures: interpreter trace == AOT trace (byte-equal).
- TC-4.2 Deliberately broken fixtures (bad opcode, dispatch miss, stack imbalance) fail loudly — no silent fallback.
- TC-4.3 `git ls-files` contains zero generated units; regenerate-twice is byte-stable (fingerprint gate).
- TC-4.4 VFPU differential fuzz: codegen-emitted VFPU vs interpreter VFPU, randomized states, bitwise compare (`vi[]` + float bits) — zero diffs on the supported op set.
**Findings (2026-10-30):** root `CMakeLists.txt` already seeded (T3) with the `yakumo` static lib + `intake_tool` target — T4 extends it. Guest memory semantics arrive with the adopted `guest_memory.hpp`; **VFPU is the one place a clean-room impulse is likely — it is not sanctioned**: adopt an MIT VFPU (sp00nznet `vfpu.c` is MIT; sal063's is mixed-license — audit first) or stop and ask before writing one.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (pipeline + memory map + dispatch contract), `docs/TESTING.md` (oracle hierarchy).
**Refs:** jessicanataliagta/PSPRecomp (core), sal063 (golden-trace layering, VFPU fuzz), snuri00 (interpreter+cache, the 10 bug classes), wizardengineer (fingerprint/census gates), sp00nznet (oracle discipline).
**Gotchas:** §7C (recompiler bug classes).

### T5 — Gungnir profile: static analysis + AOT generation
**Depends on:** T3, T4
