name: Versioned texture cache: stop re-reading and re-hashing textures per draw
description: After the word-at-a-time hash fix, battle profile still shows content_key 27.55 percent plus memmove 8.59 plus memset 6.74 percent on the guest worker: resolve_texture re-reads up to 1MB and re-hashes per draw with zero reuse. Fix: cache resolved content by cheap key with correct invalidation on VRAM writes. TextureRangeIndex::invalidate_write exists but nothing calls it; guest CPU stores via AOT fast view are the hard case (staging-buffer reuse of one address with different contents mid-frame is a real pattern, so address-only keys without write tracking would render stale). submodule: follow the red-first plus PPSSPP TexCache reference pattern from x96f24n0.
result: Per-frame validated texture dedup in StateMachine::resolve_texture. First sight per (address,params) reads, hashes (counted), decodes and retains bytes; repeats reuse on byte-exact memcmp; end_frame clears; begin_list epoch skips revalidation within one display-list run (no guest code runs mid-run) and revalidates across kicks. Fully sound: mid-frame rewrites recompute, never serve stale. Host wiring: zero-copy FastSource via raw_pointer refreshed per kick, end_frame at flip. Red-first counter test plus same_run=true mutation kill. Bench stable at ~7300 MB/s hash. Full ctest green, repository_check PASS. Device: 11fps to 20fps at 2776 draws; simpleperf content_key 27.55 to 2.8 percent, memcmp 31.7 percent gone. New top costs are memmove plus malloc (per-draw copies/allocs), filed as follow-up.

name: T11a — Input core and sceCtrl mapping
description:
Depends on: T9 (T6 for the existing sceCtrl surface). Parent T11.

Input foundation:
- Add `runtime/input/` with a source-neutral event/state model: button identity, press/release edges, analog X/Y, source (touch/gamepad/keyboard/mouse), pointer/device id.
- Feed the state into the existing sceCtrl surface: PSP button bits, analog stick, deadzone, [-128,127] clamp, pressed/edge semantics, and release-all on focus/background.
- Desktop keyboard/mouse fallback: a configurable map for d-pad, face buttons, L/R, START/SELECT and mouse buttons. This path is for desktop development only.
- Define and test a deterministic source-merge policy (for example, each button records its active sources; analog values are clamped after merge). Document the chosen policy.
- Keep the core free of Android/JNI/SDL dependencies so it is host-testable.
- Host unit tests: mapping table, deadzone/clamp, press/release edges, simultaneous sources, focus-loss release-all, unknown event no-op, deterministic merge.
- No touch overlay, haptics, gamepad profiles or remap UI in this subtask.

Reference set: Yakumo's MIT `input/touch_*`, `input/gamepad_mapping` and `bindings` are the primary mapping/semantics reference; PPSSPP's sceCtrl mapping is behavioral only (GPL, no code copied).

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): tests observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

result:
T11a complete (commit bd2d954).

- runtime/input: source-neutral slots keyed by (source, device, pointer). Buttons OR across sources; analog uses the highest-priority engaged slot (Touch, Gamepad, Keyboard, Mouse), latest pointer per source; axes clamp to [-1,1] then apply the 0.12 dead zone; make/break edges are single-consumer. No SDL/JNI/guest-memory dependency.
- sceCtrl: Read/PeekBufferPositive publish the merged pad (buttons + both sticks) and sample the make/break/press/release latch; Read/PeekLatch registered. Latch sampling point is the positive-buffer read (guest frame loop), documented in the handler.
- Desktop fallback: KeyboardMap defaults (WASD/arrows, J/K/L/I, Q/E, Return/Backspace, mouse 1-3) plus an SDL3 adapter wired into the app loop; focus loss/background releases held keys and all input.
- Red-first: tests/input/input_tests.cpp and tests/test_input.py written before runtime/input existed; first build failed on the missing input_state.cpp, then contracts went green. media_tests gained live-pad and latch contracts. Deliberate mutation (pressed edges ORed every refresh) failed "holding does not repeat the edge"; reverted.
- Gates: full suite 134/134 OK; repository_check PASS (310 files); Android clean-checkout APK test and bounded boot test link/copy the new archive.

References: TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, pinned b61852a) input/touch_controls.hpp, gamepad_mapping.hpp and bindings.hpp for source/merge terminology only (no code copied); PPSSPP Core/HLE/sceCtrl.cpp for latch make/break/press/release semantics (behavioral only, GPL, no code copied); SDL3 scancode values checked by static_assert; docs/HLE.md updated for the new sceCtrl surface.

name: T13b — Title screen and menu on device: 1x textures/text, 59.94 Hz pacing, touch + gamepad
description:
Part of T13 (plan §5, milestone M4). Owns the visual/input half of TC-13.1 on the emulator first; physical-device sign-off is T13f.

# T13b — Title screen and menu on device

**Depends on:** T13a.

**Goal.** Move from "a real game frame is presented" to "the Gungnir title screen is readable and the title menu responds to both input paths".

**Work.**
- Present guest GE output through the existing Android Vulkan swapchain at 1x: correct viewport/orientation, no unintended scaling, texture replacement loader active at 1x, text/font rendering visible. No game assets or frames in the repository.
- Implement 59.94 Hz pacing (frame = 16,683.35 µs) for `sceDisplay` VBlank and presentation, replacing the T12a pacing gap. Account for late frames explicitly (counted, no hidden sleep catch-up); expose frame time and vblank counters in the `session_stop`/periodic log.
- Verify the title screen's textures and text through the T8 replacement path at 1x. Fix rendering defects red-first; where host-testable, add a synthetic GE/texture fixture. Keep the software rasterizer as the parity oracle.
- Drive the title menu with the touch overlay and with a gamepad; verify overlay hide-on-pad, merged input into `sceCtrl`, and the title → menu → first gameplay transition. Use adb/SDL input injection, never xdotool.
- Capture a screenshot through `scripts/android/screenshot.sh`, record its SHA-256 and viewport/pacing measurements in a gitignored local milestone report. No image or hash of game content is committed; the public ledger gets counts/criteria only.
- Log zero unknown/silent NIDs at the deepest bounded run and classify every remaining gap in `docs/HLE.md`.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- `tests/ge` or a new pacing fixture: fake monotonic clock produces exact 16,683.35 µs vblank spacing, bounded catch-up, and a deliberately wrong period fails. Mutation check required.
- Synthetic title/text fixture renders through the replacement path at 1x with a pinned screenshot hash (our fixture, not game content).
- On-emulator manual evidence: title screen, touch menu navigation, gamepad menu navigation, overlay hide-on-pad, title → first gameplay transition, screenshot hash.
- Bounded-run log check: `session_stop` with `missing=0 silent=0` and a named stop cause.

**Acceptance / evidence.**
- Emulator title screen is readable at 1x and both input paths reach the first gameplay transition.
- Pacing measured and documented; no underrun or frame-pacing regression in the audio path.
- All findings recorded in `docs/BRINGUP.md` with a regression test or a tracked open defect.

**Guardrails.** Emulator evidence is bring-up, not milestone closure. No game screenshots, hashes of game files or dump identities in tracked files. No xdotool. No emulator code linked.

**Docs.** `docs/BRINGUP.md`, `docs/RENDERER.md` (1x/replacement notes), `docs/INPUT.md` (title-menu results), `docs/HLE.md` (gap table).

**Reference projects (oracles and UX patterns).**
- `hrydgard/ppsspp` (GPL-2.0-or-later) — `sceDisplay`/flip timing, texture-replacement and `textures.ini` semantics; diff oracle only, never linked.
- `BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp` (GPL-2.0-or-later, PPSSPP-derived runtime) — `tools/pace_test.py` and the screenshot/compare harness; tooling may run out-of-tree, no code vendored.
- `AdamFull/psprecore` (MIT) — frontend/pause-overlay/menu structure and renderer parity shape.
- `AdamFull/ff7ccrecomp` (MIT) — texture replacement and recordings/replays UX.
- `TeamGDB/Yakumo` (MIT) — Android frontend/overlay behavior and Vulkan texture-cache handling as a cross-check.

**Research first (required).** Before writing code, run `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Read the matching source with `gh repo read-file` / `gh repo read-dir`, never raw.githubusercontent.com. Record the references used in the task result; if a reference shapes the design, add a prose note to `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`. PPSSPP, the 3rd Birthday recomp and Metal Gear Acid 2 are behavioral oracles only — never vendored or linked — and a clean-room reimplementation of an existing format, codec or protocol is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0).
Specific first searches: `sceDisplaySetFrameBuf`, `sceDisplayWaitVblankStart`, `sceGeListEnQueue` flip semantics, `textures.ini` replacement rules; `gh search code "16683" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "59.94 Hz pacing"` and `"frame pacing Adreno"`; 3rd Birthday `tools/pace_test.py` and psprecore overlay/frontend as behavioral references. `gh search code "SCREENSHOT_HASH"` is not useful here — use our own script and hash policy.

## Progress 2026-10-31 (in progress)

**Implemented.**
- `runtime/ge/state_machine.*`: GE register/matrix/texture state, vertex decode (through and 3D), matrices/viewport, texture decode with CLUT, scissor/blend/depth/cull, triangle/strip/fan and through/non-through sprite triangulation, named gaps for alpha test, mip levels and unsupported primitives. `runtime/ge/frame_queue.*` hands the latest frame to the present thread.
- `hle_media`: every decoded GE command now feeds the state machine; draws accumulate per list and are delivered on a real `sceDisplaySetFrameBuf` flip. Gaps are counted and each kind is logged once.
- `VulkanBackend::render_swapchain_draws`: presents guest draws to the swapchain (separate pipeline cache; empty call list clears without the synthetic triangle).
- `boot_runner --frame-json/--frame-at/--frame-ppm`: dumps a frame summary and renders the captured frame with the software rasterizer for parity.
- Android entry: continuous session (`stop_at_flip=false`, pacing on), frame queue, guest-frame logging, AAudio/mixer path retained.
- Tests: `tests/ge/state_machine_tests.cpp`, `tests/test_boot.py::test_first_flip_carries_guest_geometry` (frame 60), `tests/test_session.py` still green.

**Evidence so far.**
- Host: state-machine tests OK; real frame 60 has 31 draws / 3,924 vertices / 5,796 indices, 18 textured draws, textures 512x256; software rasterization shows the gold banner and text.
- Device: session runs at ~59.94 Hz with 31 draws/frame; no session stop, no crash. `ge_gaps` ~30/frame, currently `texture_mip_levels` and `alpha_test_unsupported` (and previously `sprite_non_through`, fixed).
- Device Vulkan output is wrong: a synthetic debug quad `(0,0)-(480,272)` renders as a small rainbow rectangle at the bottom-left, ~480/3063 of the surface width.

**Root cause found.**
`runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp:1721-1722` in `recreate_swapchain()` overwrites `impl_->config.width/height` with the window/swapchain size (3063x1335). `render_swapchain_draws` uses `config.width/height` for the mesh shader's virtual coordinate space, so guest 480x272 geometry is squeezed into the bottom-left. The guest virtual size must be separate from the swapchain extent and must not be changed by resize.

**Next.**
1. Add dedicated `virtual_width/height` (default 480x272) to `VulkanBackend`; keep `config.width/height`/swapchain extent for the surface. Use virtual size for push constants; swapchain extent for viewport/scissor.
2. Verify debug quad fills the surface, then the title frame.
3. Fix the software-visible garbled text (texture/UV mapping) and alpha-test/mip gaps as needed.
4. Run touch and gamepad menu navigation, capture hashed evidence, update docs.

**Files.** `runtime/ge/state_machine.{hpp,cpp}`, `runtime/ge/frame_queue.{hpp,cpp}`, `runtime/hle/hle_media.{hpp,cpp}`, `runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.{hpp,cpp}`, `android/app/src/main/cpp/main.cpp`, `tests/ge/state_machine_tests.cpp`, `tests/hle/boot_runner.cpp`, `tests/test_boot.py`, `cmake/AndroidRuntime.cmake`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `docs/BRINGUP.md` (pending final entry).

## Progress 2026-11-01 (T13b continued)

**Presentation fixed (verified on device).**
- Guest virtual extent is now separate from the swapchain extent: `Config::virtual_width/height` (480x272) feed the mesh shader push constants, while viewport/scissor use the fitted swapchain rect. `recreate_swapchain()` no longer overwrites the guest size. `fit_viewport()` and `scale_scissor_to_extent()` carry unit tests (host `ge_vulkan_tests`).
- Android surface measures 3063x1335 with `currentTransform=ROTATE_90`. The swapchain now requests `preTransform=IDENTITY` and lets the compositor rotate; `VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR` on acquire/present is treated as success (Granite's Android policy). Previously the quad/title appeared rotated 90 degrees and squeezed into the bottom-left.
- A new frame is presented only when the frame queue has one; the swapchain is no longer cleared while waiting, which removed the black flicker between guest flips.
- Sprite expansion bug found and fixed: the bottom-left sprite vertex kept the top-left Y, so every sprite drew as a triangle. This was the garbled title text. Regression test `through_sprite_quad` in `tests/ge/state_machine_tests.cpp`. Text now renders legibly ("Checking storage media. Do not remove storage media.", publisher logo).

**Boot flow advanced to the title.**
- Savedata: after shutdown, `sceUtilitySavedataGetStatus` keeps returning 0 (NONE) instead of `WRONG_TYPE`, matching JPCSP's documented behavior; added a `started` flag. AUTOLOAD (mode 0) and AUTOSAVE (mode 1) are wired to the existing load/save paths. Kernel savedata tests extended.
- UMD: bound `sceUmdCheckMedium`, `sceUmdWaitDriveStat`, `sceUmdWaitDriveStatCB`, `sceUmdCancelWaitDriveStat`; the game stopped at `sceUmdCancelWaitDriveStat` before this.
- sceMpeg is deferred to T12/M5. All 38 sceMpeg entry points in the NID table (24 imported by this module) are now bound to explicit named-gap errors (`sceMpegInit` -> `SCE_MPEG_ERROR_NO_RAPI`, others -> `NOT_INITIALIZE`, cleanup returns success), logged as `[hle] gap: sceMpeg::...`. Without this the game skipped movies by stopping on a missing NID; with it the opening movie is skipped and boot continues.
- Scheduler fairness: after the MPEG failure the movie worker (`loopHacker`, priority 31) busy-polled `sceKernelTryReceiveMsgPipe`/`sceKernelCheckCallback` and starved `user_main` (priority 32). A provisional 50 us idle delay in `sceKernelCheckCallback` (no callbacks queued) lets the main thread run and send the worker's 0xBEEF event. Host flips rose from 310 to 476 and the game reached the title. This behavior still needs a proper contract test and a documented rationale (or replacement) before closure.

**Evidence.**
- Host: frame 450 software PPM shows the Gungnir title key art (32 draws, 21 textured); frame 60/ATLUS/logo screens render correctly. `test_boot` frame-60 assertion still green; `ge_vulkan_tests`, `ge_state_machine_tests`, `hle_kernel_tests` green with the new contracts.
- Device: storage-check text and publisher logo render upright at the correct aspect; the user confirms the title path now works. The app reports guest flips at ~20 fps on the title (60 frames per 3 s).
- Device audio is the open problem. Instrumented log at ~15 s: `pulled=670277 underrun=19741 submitted=1273 overruns=0 rejected=0 peak=0 xruns=0`. `peak=0` means every buffer reaching `MixerSink` was silent in that run, so the audible distortion reported earlier is not reproduced by this instrumentation yet. The title exercises `sceAtracDecodeData` heavily (1.18M calls in a 2.5M-dispatch host run), plus `__sceSasCore` and `sceAudioOutputPannedBlocking`; ATRAC streaming/decode and pacing are the prime suspects.

**References used.**
- PPSSPP `Common/GPU/Vulkan/VulkanContext.cpp` (preTransform/rotation), `Core/HLE/sceKernelThread.cpp` (callbacks/scheduling), `Core/HLE/sceUtility.cpp` (savedata status), `Core/Dialog/SavedataParam.h` (savedata mode enum), `GPU/Software/Sampler.cpp` (swizzle/CLUT4).
- Themaister/Granite `vulkan/wsi.cpp` (Android SUBOPTIMAL handling).
- JPCSP `sceUtility.java` (`GetStatus` keeps returning NONE after shutdown).
- jrouwe/JoltPhysics `RendererVK.cpp` (preTransform usage).
- uofw `include/video/lib_mpeg.h` (MPEG error codes), `pspdev/pspsdk` (`psputility_savedata.h`, `ThreadManForUser.S` NID confirmation).

**Next.**
1. Capture the actual PCM the device hears (mixer tap or ATRAC decode dump) and determine whether the distortion is ATRAC decode, silence/gaps, clipping or underrun stutter.
2. Fix ATRAC track decode/streaming and/or mixer pacing; re-check peak/underrun/xrun counters at the title and in the first menu.

5. Run the full suite and clean-checkout gates; update `docs/BRINGUP.md`, `docs/QA.md`, `docs/HLE.md` (MPEG gap, CheckCallback yield) and the T13b report.

## Progress 2026-11-01 (T13b audio and NEW GAME)

**Audio mixer was serialising channels.** `MixerSink` appended every channel
to one FIFO. The title feeds channel 4 (silence) and channel 5 (music) at
44.1 kHz each, so the FIFO gained ~59 k frames/s, filled, and `submit()`
returned false; the HLE stopped the session with `audio sink rejected a
buffer` at ~16 s. The serialised channels were the audible garble. The mixer
is now a timeline mixer: per-channel cursors, 32-bit summation, a 46 ms lead,
a counted resync when a channel falls behind and a counted restart when the
timeline outgrows the ring. `peak` now measures the mixed output. Red-first
evidence: the new two-channel-sum and overflow contracts fail against the HEAD
FIFO and pass with the timeline mixer.

**Descriptor pool exhaustion.** The title froze at ~16 s with
`render_failed: texture descriptor failed (-1000069000)`
(`VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_POOL_MEMORY`). The pool had 64 sets and no
`VK_DESCRIPTOR_POOL_CREATE_FREE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_BIT`, so freed texture sets
never returned. The pool is now 4096 sets with the free flag.
`ge_vulkan_tests.many_textures` uploads 96 distinct textures; it failed at
texture 63 on the old pool and passes now.

**ATRAC decode starvation.** After those fixes the picture stopped at frame
420 with `SOUND thread(UMD)` (priority 16) spinning at `0x0883AAC0` and
`user_main` (priority 32) merely ready. `sceAtracDecodeData` returned
immediately on success and on `SCE_ATRAC_BUFFER_IS_EMPTY`; the track was
opened with 128 KiB of a 959016-byte data chunk, so after 176 frames the
decode loop returned empty forever. Every decode attempt now waits for the
media engine (`1815 + bytes*158/100` us stereo ATRAC3+, `970 + bytes*44/100`
stereo ATRAC3). After the fix `user_main` runs, all sound threads wait on
audio/delay, and frames advance past the title.

**NEW GAME path.** With the mixer and decode pacing fixed, touch Cross on the
title selects NEW GAME, the game renders the difficulty screen (BASIC /
ADVANCE), and music keeps playing (`peak=23278`, `underruns=0` after startup,
`xruns=0`). The first NEW GAME transition executed
`sceSasCore::__sceSasSetADSRmode`, which used to be an unbound gap; the eight
SAS ADSR/noise/reverb controls are now bound with PSP validation (noise
silent, reverb stored but not mixed, decay always exponential).

**Current blocker.** Confirming a difficulty (Cross) faults inside guest code:
`Guest memory access outside PSP RAM/EDRAM at 0x20` at `0x088FFF64`, a0=0.
The getter at `0x088040A4` returns a null object (global at `0x08A22EF4`,
field +0x5C) and the caller dereferences `this+0x20`. This is the new-game
initialisation path, not the title/menu path.

**Still to do.** Remove the temporary `[session] heartbeat` and `atrac`
device traces, verify the D-pad hit region (centre taps are dead; the down
sector is below centre), record device QA, run the full suite and
`repository_check`, and update `docs/BRINGUP.md` / `docs/HLE.md` (already
updated for the mixer, pool, decode pacing and SAS controls).

**Verification and gates (final T13b device checkpoint).** Touch input is
verified on the M2102K1AC: Cross on the title opens the new-game path, and a
touch on the down sector of the on-screen d-pad moves the difficulty
selection (the centre is a dead zone by design). The pitch/text stays upright
and music plays with `peak=23278 overruns=0 rejected=0 xruns=0`. Final APK
SHA-256 `66d61a495a495d6491699efcfe194165a3ed938d79681d4d150cad63e7e5f419`;
device record `docs/qa/2026-11-01-t13b-title.md`. Host gates: full suite 160
tests OK (11 skipped), `tools/repository_check.py` PASS (386 files),
`git diff --check` clean. Temporary heartbeat/ATRAC tracing is removed; the
only remaining diagnostics are the one-shot session stop reason and the
AAudio stream configuration line.
result: Title screen, music, touch menu and difficulty selection verified on the M2102K1AC (Android 14, Adreno). The title key art and text render upright at the fitted 16:9 aspect; music plays with peak=23278, no rejected buffers and no xruns; touch Cross opens NEW GAME and the on-screen d-pad moves the difficulty selection. Four defects found and fixed red-first: (1) MixerSink serialised channels in one FIFO, filling it at ~59k frames/s and stopping the session ('audio sink rejected a buffer'); it is now a per-channel timeline mixer with 32-bit summation, a 46 ms lead, counted resyncs and counted overflow restarts. (4) The eight SAS ADSR/noise/reverb imports were unbound; NEW GAME executed __sceSasSetADSRmode. They are now bound with PSP validation (noise silent, reverb stored not mixed, decay always exponential). name: SDL main thread stack is at its limit and crashes at startup
description:
Adding a few hundred bytes of locals to main() crashes the app at startup: SIGSEGV in the SDLThread during asset loading, log stops after runtime_assets_current, no gungnir log line afterwards. Fault reports say the stack pointer is past the top of the stack. It reproduced twice with different small additions (the interpolation schedule, then the cadence gap counters), and reverting main.cpp to the committed state still crashed once, so the margin is effectively zero and any change can tip it.

Fix direction: find what actually consumes the SDL thread stack at startup (inlined SDL/JNI/Vulkan paths, not just main()'s frame; the disassembly showed only ~5.8 KB), then either move the remaining large loop state off the frame, or give the thread explicit headroom. Add a gate: a startup smoke that runs the app N times and fails on any crash, so this stops being intermittent.

Acceptance: the app cold-boots 10/10 on the phone with the full frame-rate work in place, no startup SIGSEGV in logcat, and the cause is named in BRINGUP.
result: Cause: verify_game_data kept std::array<unsigned char,1u<<20> as a local (1,049,040-byte frame) on the SDL thread, which the device measures at limit_kb=1043 used_kb=9. Buffer is now a heap vector. Gates: -Werror=frame-larger-than=16384 on every runtime library in both build roots (old code fails the build at 1,049,152 bytes); identity gate tested on a 512 KiB thread; stack_space thread=<name> startup diagnostic for the SDL and session threads; scripts/android/qa-startup.sh repeats the cold boot and fails on any crash. Device: runs=10 failures=0. Regression tests: game_data_tests, stack_space_tests, tests.test_startup_limits. docs/BRINGUP.md names the cause; plan 7E.9. Commit 6eb601a.

name: T9c — Game-data intake: SAF, adb path, hash gate and first-run unpack
description:
Depends on: T9a, T9b.

Implement both documented game-data paths and enforce identity before boot:
- SAF: `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT` (ISO) and/or `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE`, persist the URI permission, stream into app-private storage. No `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`.
- adb path: scan `getExternalFilesDir()/game/` for a pushed ISO. Both paths converge on one `GameData` model (source, path, size, CRC, gate status).
- Runtime hash gate: verify size + CRC32 `183F3EDC` (published disc identity) before boot. A mismatch is a named error and blocks boot, not a warning. Use zlib's `crc32`, not a hand-rolled implementation. Log the result and show it in the UI.
- First-run asset unpack with a version stamp: shaders/config/synthetic fixtures from APK assets to `filesDir` atomically; a version bump replaces them; no game assets bundled.
- Report the selected source, path, size, CRC and gate status in the UI and logcat.

Tests (red first): a synthetic ISO fixture with a known size/CRC (hand-authored bytes) passes; one-byte corruption and wrong size fail with distinct named errors; SAF copy and adb scan resolve the same model (JVM unit tests + host fixture); first-run unpack is idempotent and re-runs on a version bump. TC-9.3.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT" --extension kt`; `gh search code "takePersistableUriPermission" --extension kt`; `gh search code "getExternalFilesDir" --extension kt`; `gh search issues "SAF persisted permission lost"`; `gh search code "crc32" "iso" --extension cpp`.

Refs: Yakumo SAF picker, azazel6 hash-only identity discipline, `tools/intake/intake.py` identity gate. Gotchas: §7E.2.
result:
Added runtime/platform/android/{game_data,assets}.{hpp,cpp} and a host game_data_tests target. Discovery scans <internal>/game and <external>/game for *.iso (case-insensitive, sorted); the identity gate checks the published size (262766592) before reading and then zlib CRC32 (183F3EDC), with named errors no_game_data / game_data_open_failed / identity_size_mismatch / identity_crc_mismatch / game_data_read_failed. A corrupt candidate is skipped when a valid sibling exists; if every candidate fails, the first failure is returned.

name: Audit GE depth clear value and clear_depth_write coverage
description: Our swapchain and headless passes clear depth to 1.0f. Yakumo main GE pass clears depth to 0.0f, matching game convention (Gungnir clears depth to 0 via vertex strips under the inverted range with GREATER). A 1.0 pass clear is harmless only if every clear draw writes the plane. Steps: verify 0xD3 bit-10 decode coverage for all clear draws in the captured frame corpus; compare software Framebuffer initial depth against the Vulkan pass clear; red-first parity test proving identical plane content after clears on both backends, switching the pass clear to 0.0 if needed. Full suite plus repository_check. Acceptance: documented proof of plane equivalence plus green tests; no visual change on device. NOTE 2026-11-02: queued behind icd0chmt after battle profiling showed texture re-read/re-hash (content_key 27 percent plus copy 15 percent) dominates frame cost; depth audit unchanged otherwise.
result: Audited, no runtime change. Corpus (host boot_runner frames from battle3/save-menu/snapshot snapshots, 2670/269/2501 draws): every frame starts with draw 0 color-clear plus keep-depth, draw 1 full-plane depth clear to z=0, and a second full-plane depth clear late in heavy frames; bit-10 keeps never leave stale pixels because a full depth write always follows. The 1.0f pass clears are therefore overwritten before any depth test can read them, so switching to 0.0f would be unobservable churn. Oracle notes: Yakumo replay clears 0.0f, PPSSPP renders clear-mode draws vertex-driven like ours (no reliance on pass value). Lock: new color-observed clear-write/clear-keep parity test in ge_vulkan_tests (mutation-proven: forcing depthWriteEnable off fails it), full ctest green, repository_check PASS. boot_runner frame JSON now carries clear_depth_write for future audits.

name: T3 — Game intake pipeline (game.iso → verified local build tree)
description:
Part of 'Gungnir Recomp — Master Plan' (epic). Plan section T3 (.dex/plan.md §5).

# T3 — Game intake pipeline (`game.iso` → verified local build tree)

**Depends on:** T1
**Work:** `tools/intake/`: (1) **disc input = ISO only** (locked decision §1: `game.chd` is converted user-side via [CHDStudio](https://github.com/purelogiccode/CHDStudio) or `chdman extractcd`; intake refuses `.chd` with a named error pointing at `docs/INTAKE.md`; we never parse CHD — the identity gate *verifies, not trusts*, the converter); (2) identity gate: size 262,766,592 + CRC32 `183F3EDC`, **fail closed** on mismatch; (3) ISO9660 extract of `PSP_GAME/` tree (EBOOT.BIN, USRDIR `*.dar`, INSDIR, PARAM.SFO — verify disc ID ULUS-10592); (4) decrypt hook — **no decryption code in-repo**; invoke user-supplied pspdecrypt/PPSSPP "Dump decrypted EBOOT.BIN" out-of-process, accept `BOOT.BIN` plaintext or user-provided decrypted ELF, validate PRX shape (`e_type 0xFFA0`, `vaddr = file_offset − 0xC0`, reloc section `0x70000020`, types 2/5/6); (5) `build/game/manifest.json`: module list, SHA-256s, segments, reloc counts, NID import inventory. All outputs under `build/` (gitignored).
**Test cases:**
- TC-3.1 End-to-end on local `game.iso` produces manifest.json with expected module set. *(Covered by `tests/test_intake.py` — written and observed red before implementation.)*
- TC-3.2 Wrong-CRC input (bit-flipped ISO) aborts with named error `IDENTITY_MISMATCH`; `.chd` input aborts with named error `CHD_NOT_SUPPORTED` pointing at CHDStudio.
- TC-3.3 Truncated/decrypted-partially ELF rejected (magic + program-header checks): `~PSP` magic → `ENCRYPTED_EXECUTABLE` (points at out-of-process decrypt), truncated/garbage → `ELF_INVALID`.
- TC-3.4 Every intermediate artifact lands under `build/`; `repository_check` still green.
**Findings (2026-10-30, from implementation):** ISO9660 + ELF32 + PARAM.SFO parsing is **adopted** from TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, `third_party/yakumo/`, pin `b61852a`) — not clean-room, per §1 Code reuse. Intake shape is therefore a C++ reader tool (`tools/intake/intake_tool.cpp`, subcommands `iso-extract`/`elf-inspect`/`sfo-info`, built by root `CMakeLists.txt`) + Python orchestrator (`tools/intake/intake.py`: identity gate + manifest via stdlib `zlib`/`hashlib`/`json` — existing implementations). Known gap: vendored `elf32.cpp` handles reloc section `0x700000A0` only; Gungnir's EBOOT uses `0x70000020` — intake counts both via its own section walk (`ElfSection` list + raw entry scan), vendored code stays unpatched (recorded in `third_party/yakumo/PROVENANCE.md`). Manifest records the actual section type found, for T5.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/INTAKE.md` (user-facing: how to supply their own disc, external decrypt tools, what the gates check).
**Refs:** gungnir-ptbr (ISO offsets, `~PSP` layout — facts only), wtf-psp-recomp (`extract.ps1` report style), Yakumo (`prepare_game.sh` SHA-pin pattern), codepdbh (`--verify-only` identity gate).
**Gotchas:** §7B (format traps), §7A.1–A.3.

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1). Clean-room reimplementations of existing formats/codecs/protocols are NOT sanctioned (plan §0.6 / AGENTS.md #0) — adopt audited open-source code with provenance or stop and ask.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

EBOOT.BIN; sysdir execs covered; sha256 cross-checks), TC-3.2 wrong-CRC/sizes abort IDENTITY_MISMATCH + .chd aborted CHD_NOT_SUPPORTED with CHDStudio guidance, TC-3.3 encrypted/truncated/garbage rejected by name (ENCRYPTED_EXECUTABLE / ELF_INVALID), TC-3.4 artifacts confined to build/ + repository_check green. name: Fast-forward: R2-hold, R3 or touch FF toggle plays the game at 3x speed
description:
Fast-forward: holding gamepad R2 (right trigger), pressing R3, or toggling the FF touch ring next to SELECT runs the game at 3x; release/untoggle returns to 1x.

Why. PSP vblank is 59.94 Hz and the guest paces itself with sceDisplayWaitVblankStart(Multi) (runtime/hle/hle_media.cpp:254-296). Fast-forward must buy wall time without changing what the guest sees, or it breaks determinism, audio sync, VBlank/VTimer deadlines and T15 snapshots.

Implemented (host side, red-first):
- runtime/input/host_controls.* — HostControls with a hold (momentary) and a latch (toggle) per control, active() = hold OR latch, release_holds() on background/focus loss (latch survives suspend/resume), speed() = 1.0 idle / kFastForwardSpeed (3.0).
- Kernel pacing: set_speed_provider() feeds a pacing multiple that only scales the hold against real time (Kernel::pace_step/paced_real_us, pure and unit-tested). VBlank cadence, VTimers and every emulated deadline are unchanged; a speed change rebases the hold; real_time_of() divides the span so T17 interpolation stays honest. Wired by GameSession::start to input::host_controls().speed().
- Audio: MixerSink::set_muted() drops guest buffers while fast-forwarding, counts muted_buffers, resets the timeline (never rejected/overrun), and unmute restarts one lead ahead. main.cpp polls the control each frame and logs fast_forward active=<0|1> speed=<n>.
- Gamepad: SdlGamepad maps R2 (RIGHT_TRIGGER axis over half) to the hold and an R3 press (SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_RIGHT_STICK, only while the profile leaves it unbound) to the latch toggle, suppressed while the settings overlay is open and never published to sceCtrl; release_all/close clear holds and leave the latch.
- Touch: TouchControl::FastForward ring at (0.43, 0.08) next to SELECT latches on tap, is never a guest button, lights for any source, and layout JSON moved to version 2 with a version 1 migration that keeps user geometry and gives FF its default. HostBridge JNI + a GungnirActivity toast ("Fast-forward 3x"/"Fast-forward off") on each change; the lit ring is the persistent indicator, matching the save/load toast style.
- Intent fast_forward=<0|1> latches at start for the QA form.

Host gates: host_controls_tests, pacing_contracts in hle_kernel_tests, mixer mute contract, touch FF + v1 migration, sdl_gamepad R2/R3 (including a mapped R3 keeping its guest binding). Docs: INPUT.md, AUDIO.md, HLE.md, ANDROID.md, SNAPSHOT.md, TESTING.md, QA.md, SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md, plan §7 D.8.

Remaining (device-only, cannot close from host tests): 3x measured as game progress per wall second on the phone, no audio wedge, latch across suspend/resume, and save-state round trip while fast-forwarding — QA.md step 9, driven by T14a. No save-state format change: the speed is host state and never enters the snapshot or its identity.

Device cell 2026-11-03 (M2102K1AC, arm64, APK 520958d0…, docs/qa/2026-11-03-m2102k1ac-fastforward.md): PARTIAL PASS. 55 s bounded runs gave 3.01x vblanks and 2.99x flips per wall second; a 77 s latched battle scene kept the submitted counter frozen while muted climbed with overruns/rejected/xruns at 0, audio resumed after the latch cleared, a host snapshot saved and loaded at the same resume PC with the latch intact, and the version 1 touch layout migrated to version 2 keeping the user geometry. The gamepad half was then run on the same phone with a pad attached: R3 latches and clears (active=1 at 17:47:42, active=0 at 17:48:23, 41 s apart, so a latch rather than a hold) and R2 holds (owner-verified; the two share one control so the log shows the same transitions, and tests.test_sdl_gamepad covers the merge). Rows for the touch/pacing/audio/save-load half ran on APK 520958d0, the pad rows on APK 668b8fd1 built from b0978e1; the report records both. The same session found a pre-existing defect: backgrounding ends the guest session (tracked as eqomlp5a), which also puts the suspend/resume QA cell under re-check.
result:
Fast-forward is implemented and accepted on device.

Host side: HostControls (hold + latch, speed), kernel pacing multiplier (pace_step/paced_real_us, rebase on change, real_time_of scaled), mixer mute (counted muted_buffers, timeline reset, no overrun/rejected), session wiring. Input: R2 (right trigger over half) holds, R3 (right-stick click, only while the profile leaves it unbound) latches, FF ring next to SELECT latches by touch and lights for any source, toast on each change. Touch layout schema v2 with a v1 migration that keeps user geometry. The speed is host state and never enters a snapshot or its identity.

name: Cut per-vertex transform/shade/decode math
description: Cut per-vertex transform/shade/decode math. DONE (CPU side): pipeline by-ref plus generation-cached pipeline (red-first pipeline_cache_reuse, mutation kills). Device: 20fps, operator==/transform_state/ctor out of profile. BINDING VERDICT (TEMP flip_probe, fully reverted): 60 flips with vwaits=1 vvals=2 — the game issues essentially zero vblank waits per frame, so 20fps is NOT voluntary game pacing via waits. Guest worker averages 27 percent CPU (cumulative TIME+ delta), main thread ~15 percent visible — neither thread saturates. Render structure is sane (one pass, 2677 indexed draws, one submit) but render_swapchain_draws calls vkDeviceWaitIdle EVERY frame plus a fence wait after present — full-drain serialization, plus per-frame texture upload/create_draw_resources. Conclusion: remaining ~37ms/frame is GPU-side or present-sync, invisible to simpleperf cpu-cycles. NEXT PHASE (new work, needs GPU visibility we lack): remove per-frame waitidle with proper resource lifetimes, overlap upload/record/submit, measure with fence-timestamp or AGI gap analysis. name: Auto-save snapshot on watchdog stall
description: When the session watchdog fires (no flips for stall_seconds), the guest is usually wedged and the only evidence is the log. Reproducing then costs a full replay (20 plus minutes on device). Make the watchdog save a snapshot automatically before stopping, turning every stall into an instant post-mortem repro. Approach: in the stall path of game_session (where guest_stall is emitted and stop is requested), invoke the existing snapshot-save flow to a stall-dedicated path (for example snapshots Stall plus timestamp under the app snapshots dir), then stop as today. Must reuse the finished-session guards already used by the menu save path; failures to save must log and never break the stop itself. Include the stall metadata (seconds, flips, inflight import) in the saved record or a sidecar note. Red-first where possible: contract test that a stalled session triggers a save call with the right path and still stops; host test that a saved stall snapshot reloads. Full suite plus repository_check; verify on device by forcing a short stall timeout and confirming the snapshot file appears and reloads to the same frame. Follow-up noted but out of scope: richer progress signals beyond flips (dispatch and IO counters) to separate slow loading from true deadlock; per-game stall timeout already exists via intent. Never reference dex IDs in commits, PRs, or docs.

name: T17a.3 — Remove host-side stalls that pace the guest (audio park)
description:
Blocked by T17a.1; its numbers set the scope.

First suspect: a blocking sceAudio channel parks the guest until the mixer
drains (runtime/hle/hle_audio.cpp drain_us; the pre-battle stall report shows
exactly this park). If the guest is paced by host audio, decouple it: the mixer
already buffers, and the guest must not wait a host frame on it.
Red-first: with a full ring, N blocking submissions return in bounded time and
the guest clock does not advance by the drain; no xrun growth.

Second suspect: a deliberate guest delay (sceKernelDelayThread / CB). That is
guest behaviour and must not be shortened silently. Record it, and if the title
needs the higher rate, expose it as a named per-title option (parent option 3)
validated scene by scene, never as a global default.

Acceptance: the measured producer rate reaches what the host can present with
no audio xrun growth; any guest-visible timing change is opt-in and named;
two runs are deterministic.

## Visual gate

Timing-only change: the same battle snapshot at the same dispatch bound must
produce draw-list JSON and a frame PPM byte-identical to the T17a.1 baseline.
A pixel change means the limiter fix altered guest behaviour and the change is
rejected.

## Progress 2026-11-03 (investigation, no code)

New evidence narrows the extra vblank, and it is NOT audio-specific:

- The title-screen run in the T17a.1 measurement shows the same shape as the
  battle: waithist all at Multi(2), flipvblank = 3, waitafterflip = 1,
  flipafterwait = 0. Audio was near-silent there (peak 0 for the first
  seconds), so the 96 ms/frame of summed audio blocking is not what pushes the
  wait one vblank late.
- The 8 ms sceKernelDelayThreadCB cadence is identical on both scenes
  (6.25 calls per flip) and runs on the SAS thread.
- The HLE ring puts the flip on user_main and the following
  sceDisplayWaitVblankStartMultiCB on "SOUND thread(UMD)", with
  sceGeListSync (one per flip), sceRtcGetCurrentTick and msgpipe/UMD polling
  in between.
- The kernel only advances virtual time when every thread is blocked, so a
  thread blocked on a 5-8 ms audio/deadline cycle can move the clock forward
  in the gap between the flip and the wait.

Next experiment (cheap, no guest change): record the vblank counter at the
return of sceGeListSync and at the next vblank-wait issue, per frame, to see
which call the missing vblank lands in. If it lands in sceGeListSync, the sync
path is stalling a vblank and that is a real bug; if it lands in a delay or an
audio block on another thread, the title is deliberately pacing a 20 Hz loop
and option 3 stays the only route to a higher logic rate (interpolation already
runs on top of it).
result:
Negative result, no code change to the runtime: there is no host-side stall to remove. The extra vblank is guest pacing.

Instrumentation (commit above): a flip opens a gap that the next vblank wait closes, and every DelayThread/sceAudioOutputPannedBlocking call inside it records its requested time and the vblank delta consumed during the call. Tested in the cadence contracts (only in-gap calls count; the wait closes the gap).

Host battle snapshot, 951 flips: gap_delays=2003 (2.1 per flip), gap_delay_us=16.02 s -> 16.85 ms per frame, exactly one vblank (16.683 ms). gap_audio=2786, gap_audio_us=31.3 s, gap_audio_vblanks=500. So the title does two ~8 ms sceKernelDelayThreadCB calls per frame after the flip and then waits 2 vblanks: 1 + 2 = 3 vblanks = 19.98 fps, by the guest's own schedule. The audio drain contributes virtual time on other threads but is not what delays the wait.

Consequences:
- Do not shorten those delays: they are guest-chosen durations honoured exactly, and changing them is the logic-rate override (parent option 3), which neither PSP reference uses and this title does not need for smoothness because interpolation already runs on top of the 20 Hz source.
- The earlier 'audio park' hypothesis is retracted in favor of this measurement; the summed audio blocking is real but overlaps other threads.
- The 20 fps source is therefore a floor for T17a.8: presented rate is bounded by the present cost (~86/s measured), not by the guest.

T17a.8 is now unblocked.

name: Verify present-path staging copies are at their floor
description: vulkan_backend copies each frame's vertices/indices into mapped staging buffers (std::copy in render_headless_draws and render_swapchain_draws). Hypothesis: this is one batched copy per frame and is the irreducible floor. Steps: measure bytes per frame from the attribution subtask, confirm the copy is a single contiguous write per buffer, check for double handling (e.g. transient vectors before staging). If a redundant intermediate exists, remove it red-first with device proof; if it is already minimal, close with the measurement as evidence. Acceptance: numbers recorded, no visual change.
result: Floor verified by inspection, no code change. Staging upload in vulkan_backend (render_headless_draws/render_swapchain_draws) is one batched std::copy per buffer per frame, and it is also a layout conversion: ScreenVertex is 15 floats (60B) versus VulkanDrawVertex 12 floats (48B), so the copy cannot be removed without restructuring emit to write backend types (needs mapped-buffer lifetime at draw time; recorded as future work). Per-frame traffic about 30k verts x 48B plus indices, mandatory GPU upload. Closed with measurement.

**Docs.** `docs/BUILDING.md`, `docs/ANDROID.md`, README links.

name: T8d — Replacement loader for user PNGs at any resolution
description:
Depends on: T8a, T8c.

Load user PNG replacements from the replacement folder using the same
content key as dump mode. A replacement at any resolution (2x/4x included)
takes precedence over the guest texture; sampling follows GE state for
filter/clamp and must not assume the replacement matches native dimensions.
A PNG with no matching key is reported by name (log line, counted) rather
than silently ignored; a corrupt PNG fails closed with a named error. Dump
mode must never clobber an existing replacement.

Tests (red first):
- TC-8.2 reload half: dump -> replace -> reload in the Linux runtime with a
  synthetic scene; the replacement pixels reach the rendered frame.
- 2x and 4x replacements win over the native texture and scale correctly.
- Key mismatch is reported and leaves the native texture active.
- Corrupt PNG fails closed; removing the precedence rule fails the test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code
"<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete
implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"`
for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "texture_replacement" --extension cpp`;
`gh search code "textures.ini" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues
"texture replacement scaling"`; `gh search code "png_load" --extension cpp`.

Refs: psprecore texture_replacement.cpp (MIT, behavioral reference),
ff7ccrecomp `tools/psptex` HD layering behavior, T7 Vulkan texture upload
path. Gotchas: §7A.2, §7D.2 (bufw/CLUT correctness).
result:
Added runtime/tex/{replace.hpp,replace.cpp} and the gungnir_tex_replace target. TextureReplacements loads replace/<KEY>.png (also lowercase/.PNG) for the T8c content key, accepts any resolution, and normalises user PNGs to RGBA8 through the shared libpng reader. ReplacementImage::state_for copies the live clamp/filter state and overrides format to RGBA8, swizzle off, and width/height/buffer width to the replacement, so the GE sampling path handles 2x/4x images without a separate scaler. Successful loads are cached until clear()/set_root(); native textures remain the fallback.

find() fails closed with named errors: invalid_root, invalid_key, not_found, file_access_failed, invalid_replacement, and PNG errors (png_read_failed/png_unsupported_layout/file_not_found). scan(known_keys) reports present PNGs, loaded known keys, unmatched PNG filenames (sorted) and per-file errors (sorted), so unknown/corrupt files are counted rather than dropped. Dump mode never writes under replace/.

Tests in tests/tex/replace_tests.cpp: 2x and 4x replacements rendered through the software rasterizer with the expected block pattern, native fallback, state derivation and clamp/filter copying, unmatched/corrupt scan reporting, cache/clear reload, dump/replacement isolation, missing replace directory and invalid keys/roots. Mutation: dropping the replacement width/height fails 'replacement state uses the image dimensions'. Local check: a 256x56 container texture dumped and loaded as a 512x112 replacement (scan loaded=1, no errors). Full suite 78/78 green; repository_check PASS (227 files).

References used: psprecore runtime/src/gpu/texture_replacement.cpp (MIT) for 16-hex keyed folder scanning, any-resolution PNG loading and cache/worker shape (behavior only; no code copied), PPSSPP PR #8715, the texture-replacement wiki and GPU/Common/TextureReplacer.cpp for pack semantics (hashranges/filtering/mipmaps remain unimplemented; no code adopted), LiinkPK/Texture-Replacement-Tool-for-PPSSPP for pack workflow (binary-only), the T8c content key, and libpng for decoding. docs/TEXTURE_REPLACEMENT.md now documents the replace/ layout, key rules, API, errors, cache/reload and dump isolation.

commit.message: Add user PNG texture replacements

name: T17a.5 — Match and interpolate draws (renderer interpolation)
description:
Given the record from T17a.4, produce an in-between draw list at parameter t:
- match by key, then occurrence order;
- reject implausible partners: an average screen-space delta above the cut
  threshold leaves both draws uninterpolated, so a camera cut never smears
  (Chinatown Wars rejects above 0.5; The 3rd Birthday treats 0.3 screen widths
  as a cut);
- lerp x, y, z and inv_w and leave colour, texcoord and state untouched. This
  is the Chinatown Wars vertex-midpoint method, which maps directly onto our
  final screen-space vertices; the 3rd Birthday matrix reprojection needs
  per-draw matrices we do not keep and is the fallback if midpoint looks wrong
  on skinned or scrolling content;
- cap the recorded draws of a frame that never sees FINISH (named, logged), and
  log the match percentage.

Red-first: a synthetic two-frame pan interpolates its midpoint within tolerance;
an unmatched draw passes through unchanged; a through (2D/HUD) draw is never
interpolated; the cut guard rejects a jump over the threshold.
Mutation: break matching and confirm the pass-through test dies.

## Visual gate

Real frames are untouched: the in-between list is additional output, so the
real frame still matches the baseline PPM/JSON exactly. A synthetic two-frame
pan renders its midpoint within tolerance, an unmatched draw renders as the
current frame, and a through-mode HUD draw is identical to the baseline in both
presents.
result:
The interpolation pass is implemented and unit-tested (commit on top of 91dbf19).

runtime/ge/frame_interpolation.* gains InterpolationStats and interpolate_frame(frame, history, t): matched transform draws move to t of the way from the previous frame to this one, positions only (x, y, z, inv_w); colour, texture coordinates and state stay the frame's own. This is the Chinatown Wars vertex-midpoint method, which fits our pipeline because ge::Draw already holds final screen-space vertices; The 3rd Birthday's matrix reprojection needs per-draw matrices we do not keep and is recorded as the fallback if midpoint looks wrong on skinned content.

Three cases are left exactly as the guest produced them: through/2D/HUD draws (never candidates), draws with no partner (counted unmatched), and pairs whose average screen-space motion exceeds kCutScreenFraction = 0.2 of the 480-wide frame (counted as cut, so a camera cut snaps). Occurrence order keeps repeated tiles matched to their own previous draw. No cap is needed for a frame without FINISH: our pipeline flushes at every flip.

Tests: tests/ge/interpolation_tests.cpp - midpoint pan within 0.001, t=0 and t=1 reproduce the previous/current frame exactly, unmatched pass-through, through draws are not even candidates, cut rejection leaves the pair untouched, two occurrences interpolate with their own partners. Wired into test_ge_suite; GE and HLE suites plus repository_check green. Mutation check: making match() ignore the occurrence kills the occurrence contract for that reason.

Visual gate: the pass is not wired into presentation yet (that is T17a.6), so the battle baseline frame PPM remains byte-identical (3b142a21...), confirming real frames are untouched.

commit.message: Interpolate matched draws between two real frames

name: T11f — Gamepad navigation for the Menu overlay
description:
Post-closure follow-up: created after T11 was closed (T11e, 2026-10-31), so it is tracked at the top level rather than under the completed T11.

Own the Menu overlay from a paired gamepad (T11 input home; milestone needs touch + gamepad menu nav, plan QA script line 412).\n\nScope:\n- Home/back button opens the Menu overlay (when closed); Back closes it (when open). No change to touch behavior.\n- D-pad up/down moves a visible selection highlight across rows; A (cross) activates the highlighted row (same Listener path as touch taps).\n- Works from any menu state (including scrolled position); selection wraps or clamps — decide in slice plan, document it.\n- Reference discovery first per AGENTS.md (gh search code/issues for Android gamepad key handling + overlay focus semantics); record refs in SOURCE_PROVENANCE if external behavior is mirrored.\n- Red-first: host-testable contracts (key mapping, selection model) before wiring; device QA on the physical phone with a paired pad (menu fully operable without touching the screen; touch overlay hide-on-pad unchanged).\nAcceptance: full menu operable from pad alone on device (open, navigate every row incl. scrolled ones, activate Save/Load state + Reset to title + Close); touch path unchanged; qa record filed; suite green.

## Slice plan (2026-11-01)

Decisions:
- **Clamp, not wrap**, at the first and last row: predictable on a settings list, and it keeps "Reset to title"/"Close" from being one accidental press away from "Edit touch layout".
- **Buttons**: Back (SDL BACK) and Guide/Home (SDL GUIDE) toggle the overlay; D-pad up/down move; South/Cross (SDL SOUTH) activates the highlighted row.
- **Edge-triggered**: one action per press, no auto-repeat in this slice (a hold does not scroll). Rapid presses coalesce to at most one action per poll.
- **Model location**: the navigation state machine lives in `runtime/input/menu_navigation.{hpp,cpp}` (pure C++, no SDL/Java) so key mapping, clamping and the open/closed gate run under the host tests. Java owns only the highlight, scroll-into-view and invoking the existing row Listener.
- **Delivery**: Java polls `nativeMenuPoll()` on the UI thread via `Choreographer` while the activity is resumed; `nativeMenuBegin(row_count)` on show and `nativeMenuEnd()` on hide reset/drain the state. No native-to-Java callback, matching the existing Java-side gamepad polling pattern.
- **Guest input**: this slice does not suppress the pad's normal PSP mapping while the overlay is open; Back therefore also reaches the guest as Select. Documented as a known gap, to be decided during device QA (touch input is suppressed while the overlay is open, so the asymmetry is visible).
- Emulator smoke is allowed; closure still needs the paired-pad phone QA (android/AGENTS.md).

## Implementation (2026-11-01)

Host-testable slice is in place; device QA is the remaining gate.

- `runtime/input/menu_navigation.{hpp,cpp}`: Back/Guide emit Toggle, d-pad emits Move with a clamp at both ends, South emits Activate at the highlighted row. Closed state ignores move/activate. Pending queue is bounded to 8 events (oldest dropped) so a stalled UI cannot grow it.
- `runtime/platform/sdl_gamepad.cpp`: button-down edges feed the model; remap mode is excluded so the wizard cannot open the menu. No suppression of the normal PSP mapping yet (named gap in docs/INPUT.md).
- `android/app/src/main/cpp/main.cpp`: `nativeMenuBegin(rows)`, `nativeMenuEnd()`, `nativeMenuPoll()` (action in the low byte, index in the next).
- `GungnirActivity`: frame-callback poll while resumed; Toggle opens/closes, Move sets the selection, Activate runs the row. Show/hide call begin/end; the Gamepad dialog and Back now go through closeSettings.
- `SettingsOverlayView`: row/action lists, `setSelection` (clamp, highlight, scroll into view), `activateSelection` through the existing Listener path.
- Tests: `tests/input/menu_navigation_tests.cpp` (red first: missing header), virtual-pad contracts in `tests/input/sdl_gamepad_tests.cpp`, `tests/test_menu_navigation.py` including the Android CMake source-list check that caught the first link failure. `tests.test_input_suite` and `tests.test_android_app` green; `repository_check` PASS (407 files); Android debug APK builds.
- Evidence is host-only so far. Emulator smoke was not attempted: `adb shell input keyevent` does not present a gamepad device to SDL, and no host-pad or uinput injection is wired.

Remaining: paired-pad QA on the physical phone — open with Back/Guide, navigate every row including the scrolled bottom rows, activate Save state, Load state, Reset to title and Close, confirm touch still works and the touch overlay hide-on-pad behaviour is unchanged; file the QA record; then close.
result:
Device QA passed for the navigation slice (M2102K1AC, 8BitDo Lite 2, profile default).

- Back opens/closes; the first row is selected on open.
- D-pad produced every index 1..8 with a clamp at 8 and back to 0; the list scrolls. The one-per-frame poll was replaced by a full drain, fixing the thinned presses.
- Cross activated Close (8), Reset to title (7) and Load state (6) through the existing Listener path. Load state no longer falls through to the game.
- Suppression: Back/Guide are reserved and d-pad/Cross are withheld while the overlay is open; gameplay input returns on close.
- Touch still opens the overlay and activates the Gamepad row (verified with adb tap); handlers unchanged.
- Save state was skipped at the user's request to preserve their snapshot. The file was backed up and restored byte-for-byte (hash verified) before skipping; the row shares the activation path with Load state. Recorded as a deliberate gap.
- Residuals: no auto-repeat; Select cannot be bound to Back/Guide; eight-event queue bound.

Evidence: docs/qa/2026-11-01-t11f-menu-navigation.md and gitignored build/qa/2026-11-01-t11f/.

name: Attribute remaining copies with heap and call-graph profiling
description: Before further cuts: the flat profile is diffuse (no owner above 5 percent except memmove 6.6 percent). Run heapprofd (or simpleperf dwarf call-graph) on the battle scene to attribute per-frame malloc/memcpy bytes to callsites: pending suspects are Vulkan staging std::copy in vulkan_backend render_headless_draws/render_swapchain_draws, unordered_map find/insert churn in resolve_texture, jemalloc tcache contention (pthread_mutex_trylock 1.8 percent). name: T12b — Savedata and DAR asset support
description:
Part of 'Gungnir Recomp — Master Plan' (epic). Plan section T12b (.dex/plan.md §5); the parent T12 is split into audio (T12a) and savedata/DAR (T12b).

# T12b — Savedata and DAR asset support

**Depends on:** T6 (T6k savedata SIZES/dialog state machine already landed)
**Work:** (1) `runtime/savedata/`: virtual memstick `PSP/SAVEDATA/<title>/` with PARAM.SFO v1.1 (PSF) read/write and a PPSSPP-compatible layout (saves interchangeable with emulator/hardware); complete the savedata modes the title executes beyond the T6k SIZES slice; KIRK save encryption **deferred**, documented honestly (hash-left-zero stance — never ship key material). (2) `tools/dar.py` for the asset pipeline (both DAR sides: read/list/extract + in-place rewrite rules; `stored_size==0` = uncompressed). Size-preserving in-place rewrite with zero-filled tail and named errors; every writer proves a byte-identical round-trip before it may write a new payload. A host compatibility harness mounts the user's PPSSPP memstick exports read-only and copies them into a scratch root so tests never mutate the originals.
**Test cases:**
- TC-12.3 Save→load round-trip byte-stable; PARAM.SFO opens in PPSSPP.
- TC-12.4 `dar.py` lists/extracts the user's `ini.dar`; a repack round-trips byte-identically; the `stored_size==0` entries survive.
- TC-12.5 PPSSPP memstick interchange: copy the user's exported saves (`savestates/ULUS10592GUN9THSYS` and `savestates/ULUS10592GUN9THSTORY00`) into a scratch `ms0:/PSP/SAVEDATA/` root, list both through the virtual memstick, parse each PARAM.SFO, and parse→serialize each file byte-identically; then save→load→save leaves every save file byte-identical. The export is never mutated in place. A save written by our runtime into PPSSPP's memstick is listed and loadable by PPSSPP (oracle).
- TC-12.6 PPSSPP oracle: use a PPSSPP 1.20.4 clean boot (the supplied `.ppst` resumes before a battle, where no save menu exists) to list and load the exported SYSTEM/STORY saves (`ULUS10592GUN9THSYS`, `ULUS10592GUN9THSTORY00`, 61,888-byte STORY), then repeat with the tree rewritten by `SaveStore`; every rewritten file is SHA-256-identical to the export. The `.ppst` container is PPSSPP-specific and is never parsed in-repo (a clean-room reimplementation needs explicit sign-off). Evidence: `docs/qa/2026-10-31-t12b-savedata.md`.
**Local fixtures:** the exported savestate and both memstick saves live under gitignored `savestates/`; they are the user's own data, never committed, copied into a temp memstick for tests, and any case that needs them skips with the named reason `savedata_fixture_missing` when absent.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/SAVEDATA.md`, `docs/formats/DAR.md` (extended from T3/T8).
**Refs:** sal063 (savedata.c/PARAM.SFO), gungnir-ptbr (DAR traps), psprecore (`hle_savedata.cpp` SceUtilitySavedataParam offsets/modes — MIT; its save layout omits the `PSP/` prefix), PPSSPP (PARAM.SFO/save-layout oracle, behavioral only — no code).
**Gotchas:** §7B.1 (DAR `stored_size==0`), §7B.2 (in-place rewrite), §7B.3 (script `.bin` sizes), §7B.4 (both-endian ISO sizes).

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): test cases observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Device validation: see `android/AGENTS.md` — emulator is for initial bring-up; physical arm64 phone QA is required at sprint end and recorded in `docs/qa/`. Reproducible emulator: `scripts/android/emulator.sh`.
result:
T12b complete (savedata 5d78197, DAR c2123f1, PPSSPP oracle 414d9a1).

- `runtime/savedata/save_store.*`: PSP/SAVEDATA layout with validated names, symlink rejection, sorted listings, atomic per-file writes and the vendored MIT PARAM.SFO reader/writer. The SFO carries TITLE, SAVEDATA_TITLE, SAVEDATA_DETAIL, PARENTAL_LEVEL, CATEGORY=MS, SAVEDATA_DIRECTORY, the 99-entry file list and zeroed SAVEDATA_PARAMS; parse->serialize is byte-identical for exported PSP saves.
- sceUtilitySavedata implements SIZES plus LOAD (SFO fields, bind=1021, data/icons) and SAVE (data, icons/pic/snd, fresh SFO) with named PSP error codes. LIST/DELETE/picker modes remain documented gaps.
- `tools/dar.py` lists, extracts and size-preservingly repacks DAR archives: nested names, zlib and stored payloads, stored_size==0, zero-filled tails, unchanged-entry byte identity and named failures (traversal, oversized blob, stored-size change). The user's INI.DAR round-trips with an unchanged hash.
- Test cases: TC-12.3 save/load byte-stable and SFO round-trip; TC-12.4 DAR list/extract/repack with byte-identical untouched and real-archive runs; TC-12.5 exported PPSSPP saves mount/list/parse/rewrite byte-identically; TC-12.6 a PPSSPP 1.20.4 clean boot lists and loads ULUS10592GUN9THSYS and ULUS10592GUN9THSTORY00 (61,888-byte STORY) and loads the tree rewritten by SaveStore; every rewritten file is SHA-256-identical to the export. A savestate boot resumes before a battle and is not a load oracle.
- Docs: docs/SAVEDATA.md, docs/formats/DAR.md, docs/qa/2026-10-31-t12b-savedata.md.
- Named gaps: KIRK/secure save encryption and real-PSP secure saves are deferred; LIST/DELETE/picker modes are not implemented; the Android memory-stick root is wired with the HLE in T13.

name: Research first — T15a
description:
First step for T15. Complete this before writing any snapshot/restore code.

Start with:
  gh search code "SaveState" --extension cpp
  gh search code "savestate" --extension cpp
  gh repo read-file "Core/SaveState.cpp" --repo hrydgard/ppsspp
  gh repo read-dir "Core/SaveState" --repo hrydgard/ppsspp
  gh search issues --repo hrydgard/ppsspp "save state"
  gh search code "serialize" "threads" --extension cpp
Review psprecore/ff7ccrecomp and azazel6 for snapshot shape and evidence discipline.

Answer these before coding:
1. Which state does a correct PSP snapshot need? Compare against the section list in
   T15 and list what is missing or unnecessary.
2. Does PPSSPP restart the audio/GPU caches on load, and how does it report that to the
   user? That decision informs our "derived state is rebuilt" rule.
3. How are kernel objects and timers re-linked by identity on load (indices vs handles)?
4. Is there an existing container we can use instead of writing a format (AGENTS #0)?
5. What are the failure modes (version skew, corpus mismatch, partial write) and how
   does the reference fail closed?

Record: project/license + file/URL, adopted/rejected, and the decision per question. Add
a prose note to docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md when a reference shapes the design. T15 stays
blocked until this is completed.
result:
Research complete; no code written.

**Q1 — what a PSP snapshot needs.** PPSSPP's `SaveStart::DoState` quiesces the
system first (utility IO, SAS mixer, async IO, flush GPU drawing), then writes:
RAM, core timing (virtual clock), memory stick, MIPS CPU, HLE modules, kernel
objects/threads/alarms/VTimers/event flags/mailboxes/modules/msgpipes/mutexes/
semaphores, filesystem descriptors last ("kernel object destructors might close
open files"), then MMIO and the media engine. Versus T15's list: add the
virtual clock with absolute timer deadlines, interrupt state and the module
registry; drop MMIO and ME (unused here). The virtual memory stick is a host
directory, so savedata is deliberately outside the snapshot and must be
documented as such.

**Q2 — audio and GPU on load.** The GPU flushes pending drawing before a save
and resets its caches on load; the audio *device* stream is restarted while the
HLE channel state is serialized (reserved, sample address/count, volumes,
format, remaining samples, parked waiting thread/address/volumes). So
"derived caches are rebuilt, HLE state is saved" matches the reference.

**Q3 — object identity.** The kernel object pool and each subsystem's maps are
written in order and UIDs are restored verbatim; nothing is renumbered. Our
SceUID-keyed maps can be written as-is provided ID allocation stays
deterministic and load rejects duplicate IDs.

**Q4 — container.** The reference uses a Dolphin-derived chunk writer (versioned
sections with 16-byte titles) that is GPL code with no public spec. Decision:
do not copy or reverse-engineer it; define a minimal TLV container of our own
(magic, version, corpus/config identity, per-section tag+length, trailing
payload hash). That does not reimplement an existing format (AGENTS #0).

**Q5 — failure modes.** The reference validates title/version, warns when a
state was written by an older build, and on a partial or failed load clears the
JIT cache and refuses to keep the loaded state. Ours: reject on corpus hash,
config or version mismatch, verify each section hash, write atomically (temp +
rename) and never leave a half-restored session.

Also recorded: PPSSPP's `AudioChannel::DoState` keeps a compatibility fix for a
save that stored `waitingThread = -1`, which left a channel busy forever — the
same shape as the pre-battle stall hypothesis.

References recorded in `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md` (T15 section).

name: Per-title camera hook: widen the guest's culling
description:
Adaptive widescreen widens the host projection, but the guest still culls its own 3D against the native 480x272 frustum, so geometry outside it is never submitted and the widened columns show only the stretched 2D backdrop. Recovering real content needs a per-title hook into the guest's camera/culling values, not a renderer change.

Shape:
- Identify how Gungnir derives its horizontal cull bounds per scene (frustum planes, bounding-sphere tests, or a fixed screen-space margin) and where the camera's aspect/extent constant lives. Expect it in the title's own code, reached from the recompiled corpus, so the hook must be an explicit, named, gitignored per-title profile entry (same policy as the logic-rate override: opt-in, validated scene by scene), never a heuristic that silently patches arbitrary writes.
- Apply it host-side by scaling the culling extent about the view centre so the guest submits the extra columns; the host projection widening already exists (T16a).
- Fallback: when the profile has no hook, keep today's behaviour (widened frame + stretched backdrop) and count it: the periodic log must say which mode is active and how many extra columns are backdrop-only.
- Validation: A/B the same snapshot with and without the hook at a scene with visible side content; screenshots by hash only; confirm no object popping or flicker from partially culled geometry at the seam, and that nothing changes when the hook is absent.

Context: gbarecomp solves the equivalent problem per title by rebuilding the object/field view from guest RAM; on PSP the equivalent is a camera/cull hook, because the recompiled code owns the transform pipeline. Research first: record how the title culls (tooling pointers in docs/BRINGUP.md and the corpus symbols), then implement. Red-first: a host test for the extent scaling and for the profile gating, plus a device A/B recorded in docs/qa/.

name: T17a.6 — Present in-between frames at the display rate
description:
With the produced-frame timestamps from T17a.2, compute t from the wall time
between frame N and N+1 and present the interpolated list at every display
refresh in between: one in-between at 2x, three at 4x (The 3rd Birthday's own
next step was interpolating at the display rate rather than a single midpoint).

Latency is one guest interval by construction; record it and keep it constant,
never accumulating across frames. A 20-25 Hz source on a 120 Hz panel gets the
right number of in-betweens from elapsed time, not a hardcoded 0.5.

Red-first: injected-time schedule test - a 50 ms guest interval at 120 Hz
produces the expected presents with monotonic t, the real frame lands on its own
deadline, and a late or duplicate frame never presents twice.
Mutation: break the t computation and confirm the schedule test fails.

## Visual gate

On the phone, a recording of the battle shows the real frames unchanged
(compared against baseline hashes taken at the same guest frames) with distinct
in-between frames between them; the number of presents per guest interval
matches the display rate. A still frame with the scheduler stalled must not
show a torn or repeated in-between.

## Progress 2026-11-03 (work in progress, commit da5de2d)

Integration landed behind a default-off toggle: a guest frame starts a display
window and the presenter shows interpolate(previous, current, t) at each display
tick; the real frame lands at the end of the window (one guest interval of
latency by construction). Toggle = settings row persisted in preferences +
HostBridge.setFrameInterpolation + frame_interpolation intent extra.

Measured on M2102K1AC (120 Hz panel, battle snapshot):
- interpolated=599, held=9 over ~300 guest frames (~2 in-betweens per frame);
- present cost rose from 9.5 to 13.7 ms (the scratch copy plus 26k vertices);
- about 72 presented frames per second, and late_ticks == presents: every
  refresh tick is skipped because a 2834-draw present cannot meet 120 Hz;
- 44 percent of real frames are taken late behind an in-between.

Remaining before this task can close:
1. The red-first injected-time schedule test (numbers of presents per guest
   interval, monotonic t, the real frame on its deadline, no present twice).
2. The present-cost ceiling: 72 fps is bounded by the 13.7 ms present, not by
   the schedule. Either cut the per-present cost (batch/retain resources; the
   scratch copy itself is ~3.5 ms) or accept and document the ceiling, then set
   the target in T17a.8 from what the device can actually do.
3. Do not carry the scratch copy on the heap per tick without measuring; a
   reusable buffer or interpolating directly into a vertex staging buffer is
   the obvious next cut.
4. main() stack: the schedule had to move to static storage because the added
   locals overflowed the SDL thread stack (SIGSEGV in fread during startup).
   Any further main() locals need the same care.
result:
In-between presentation is implemented, host-tested and measured (commits da5de2d, plus the schedule extraction).

runtime/ge/present_schedule.* owns the timing with injected time: PresentSchedule::on_guest_frame starts a display window per guest frame (length = the previous guest interval), due() answers one present per refresh with t = elapsed/window, returns Held at the end so the real frame is shown rather than extrapolating, and counts skipped refreshes instead of bursting. The Android loop only keeps the frames: on arrival it pushes the previous frame into FrameHistory, and the tick path interpolates into a scratch buffer. Invalidated on snapshot load, reset to title and background resume, so no in-between bridges a discontinuity.

UI: Settings row Frame interpolation On/Off (persisted, HostBridge.setFrameInterpolation), frame_interpolation intent extra for QA, periodic log line interpolation active/interpolated/held/skipped_ticks. Default off.

GE and HLE suites plus repository_check green.

Device (M2102K1AC, 120 Hz, battle snapshot, interpolation on): interpolated=584, held=1 over 299 guest frames, present cost 10.1 ms, about 86 presents per second versus the guest's 20 - a 4.3x smoothing increase. Screenshot of the battle is correct with no smearing. Ceiling recorded: a 2834-draw present costs 10.1 ms, so 120 Hz is out of reach (99 presents/s maximum before loop work); skipped_ticks shows the shortfall and is the input for the present-cost work in T17a.3/T17a.8 rather than an unstated gap.

Stack finding: the interpolation state lives at file scope because the added main() locals overflowed the SDL thread stack and crashed startup in fread with no log line past runtime_assets_current.
