name: T16b — Fill-screen presentation: stretch, crop or fit
description:
Add a display-layout policy so the game can fill the phone screen instead of
letterboxing. Presentation only: the guest still produces 480x272 and no
projection or snapshot state changes.

## Research update 2026-11-03 (code-grounded; sequence and anchors fixed)

Sequencing: do this task BEFORE T16a. Both tasks edit `fit_viewport`,
`scale_scissor_to_extent`, the same two call sites (`vulkan_backend.cpp:2109`,
`:2122`), `VulkanBackend::Config` (`main.cpp:796`) and the intent-extra
surface. T16a's "presentation fills the target" is this task's policy work;
T16b owns the policy enum and T16a consumes it (`virtual_width` becomes the
effective width). Doing them concurrently guarantees conflicts.

Current anchors (the task's line numbers are stale):

- `fit_viewport` `runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp:358` (decl
  `vulkan_backend.hpp:124`); `scale_scissor_to_extent` `:377`.
- Call sites `:2109` (fit) and `:2122` (scissor), applied at `:2111`/`:2113`;
  scissor offset+clamp `:2123-2127`.
- Shader normalization `assets/shaders/ge/mesh.vert:31` against the pushed
  viewport (`vulkan_backend.cpp:2114`, `:2145`).
- `present_guest_frame` `android/app/src/main/cpp/main.cpp:246`; backend
  config `main.cpp:796`; intent helpers `main.cpp:178`/`:211`.
- Touch overlay: JNI `main.cpp:552`, Java `TouchOverlayView.java:177`
  (`updateViewport`), drawing `TouchOverlayView.java:228`.

Two findings change the task text:

- Crop must clamp its scissor to the surface. `VkRect2D` scissor offsets are
  required to be non-negative (`VUID-vkCmdSetScissor-x-00595`). Crop returns
  an oversized rect with a negative origin, and the current code offsets the
  scissor by `fitted.x/y` and never re-clamps, so crop as described would
  record invalid scissors. Clip to `[0, extent]` after offsetting and drop
  empty rects.
- The touch overlay has no guest-pixel mapping. `TouchOverlay::set_viewport`
  (`runtime/input/touch_overlay.cpp:80`) takes window size plus safe-area
  insets; controls are drawn and hit-tested in window space from normalized
  placements. No tap is converted to a guest coordinate, so "a tap maps to
  the same guest pixel in fit and stretch" describes behaviour that does not
  exist. Re-scope the input item to the real question: should controls be
  anchored to the presented image rect instead of the window, so they do not
  float over black bars in fit/crop? If no, say so in the result and drop the
  touch test.

## Deliverables

1. Config: `display_layout` = fit (default, current behaviour) / stretch /
   crop in `VulkanBackend::Config`, an Android intent extra and a
   `SettingsOverlayView` row. Unknown policy fails with a named error.
2. Presentation: teach `fit_viewport` the three policies and keep
   `scale_scissor_to_extent` and its call sites consistent. `fit` is
   today's aspect-preserving centred rect. `stretch` maps 480x272 to the
   full target (non-uniform). `crop` returns an oversized uniform rect that
   the surface clips, with the scissor clamped to the surface after
   offsetting.
3. Input: decide the overlay-anchoring question above and implement it (or
   record why fit/stretch/crop leave the window-space overlay unchanged).
4. Docs: `docs/RENDERER.md` describing fit/stretch/crop and the
   distortion/clipping trade-off, `docs/ANDROID.md` for the intent/settings
   row, and the measured 19.5:9 numbers (stretch is ~23% horizontal
   magnification; crop loses ~20% of frame height, ~10% top and bottom).
5. No snapshot involvement: presentation must not enter the T15 config hash,
   and changing it must never invalidate a snapshot.

## Red-first tests

`tests/ge/vulkan_tests.cpp`:

- stretch maps 480x272 onto a 2400x1080 target with the full rect and a
  known vertex at the expected pixel;
- crop returns a rect that covers the target and clips uniformly, and its
  scissor never has a negative offset;
- fit results are unchanged from today;
- scissor scaling under stretch is non-uniform and stays in bounds;
- an unknown policy is a named error.

`tests/input/touch_overlay_tests.cpp` only if the anchoring decision changes
the mapping.

Mutation: swap the x/y scale in stretch and confirm the mapping test fails
for that reason.

## Acceptance

Device screenshots of all three modes at 19.5:9, with HUD clipping visible
only in crop and documented; no input regression; `repository_check` PASS;
full suite green; QA evidence under gitignored `build/qa/`.

## References

`Research first — T16b` (PPSSPP `PresentationCommon`/`DisplayLayoutScreen`,
DuckStation, Chinatown Wars `hud_scale`), plus
`VUID-vkCmdSetScissor-x-00595`. Behavioral reference only; no code copied.
result: Delivered: DisplayLayout (fit/stretch/crop) in VulkanBackend::Config with present_rect, parse_display_layout (unknown -> named error, layout unchanged) and clamp_scissor_to_target; the present path uses the policy and clamps scissors to the surface after offsetting (Vulkan forbids negative scissor origins, which crop produces). Shell: --es display_layout, SettingsOverlayView 'Screen fill' row cycling Fit/Stretch/Crop with a toast, persisted, QA intent wins over the persisted value, JNI nativeSetDisplayLayout/displayLayout, and backend.set_display_layout applied each present. Tests: ge_vulkan_tests geometry (fit unchanged, stretch fills, crop overflows uniformly, scissor clamp/drop, negative origin forbidden, named error) with the stylized mutation (transposed stretch) failing exactly that contract; tests/test_display_layout.py for the shell surfaces and snapshot purity. Device (3063x1335 target, 2.29:1): fit 2356x1335 at x=353 (22.9% bars), stretch fills (1.30x horizontal magnification, distortion visible), crop 3063x1736 at y=-200 (23% of height clipped, party bar and unit banner cut). Row cycle, toast and persistence verified with the user watching. Docs: RENDERER.md presentation section incl. the touch-overlay decision (controls stay window-space: there is no guest-pixel mapping, and anchoring them to the image would move them off the bars and break existing layouts), ANDROID.md option, QA report docs/qa/2026-11-04-m2102k1ac-screen-fill.md. Judgment recorded: crop is a zoom and is not a substitute for projection widening, which is the next task.

name: Snapshot-save thread never exits and burns a core
description: Menu Save state spawns a Java thread named snapshot-save running nativeSaveSnapshot. After the save completes (snapshot_saved logged) and the session resumes, the thread stays alive and consumes ~85-90 percent of a core indefinitely (top: 4-5 min CPU time and rising). Reproduced 2026-11-02: user tapped Menu Save state at 15:07:37; two snapshot-save threads existed afterwards (one spinning at 88 percent, one idle); a VM stack dump was not obtainable without root. UPDATE 2026-11-02: mega-probe built and deployed (worker_enter/exit by kernel tid plus snap/load/reset stage tracing with finished/joinable state; build deployed 16:37 as pid 5480, TEMP in android/app/src/main/cpp/main.cpp, uncommitted). Fresh-process check EXONERATED the spinner for the current lag: no snapshot-save threads present, guest worker itself at 100 percent; true cause was per-draw texture hashing (see completed x96f24n0). Spinner leak itself is still real and untriggered on this build. NEXT: on user go, Menu Save state twice on pid 5480, read snap_* stages by tid plus top threads to locate the stuck thread end, fix lifecycle, red-first regression test if host-reproducible.
result: No defect: exonerated by kernel-tid tracing on 2026-11-02 (pid 5480). Both Menu Save states ran snap_enter to snap_exit cleanly; each old worker logged worker_exit before the join and the relaunched worker logged worker_enter after; the finished Java tids (568, 869) are gone from the thread list. The burning snapshot-save thread (tid 887, 85 percent) IS the relaunched guest worker and the idle one (tid 888, zero CPU) is the session watchdog: both inherit the creator thread's pthread name because the worker is launched from the save path. The original 15:07 pair fits identically (hot worker slowed by the since-fixed texture hash plus idle watchdog). Frames flow throughout (11fps at 2776 draws). Optional follow-up: pthread_setname_np on the worker and watchdog so future tops are unambiguous.

name: T13e — Hygiene gates: dummy ISO/ELF commit block, secret scan, license/notice, SPDX/REUSE
description:
Part of T13 (plan §5). Owns TC-13.3 and the merge-blocking hygiene matrix; depends on T13d for the CI surface.

# T13e — Hygiene gates

**Depends on:** T13d.

**Goal.** A deliberate game-artifact commit is blocked locally and in CI, and the tree proves license/notice/SPDX coverage without leaking secrets.

**Work.**
- TC-13.3: add a local regression that creates a temporary git repo, stages a dummy `.iso`/`.elf` and a `~PSP` blob, and asserts `tools/repository_check.py` fails with the recognized magic; run the same scenario in CI. Keep the real tree's `.gitignore` probes intact.
- Add a secret scan (gitleaks or equivalent, pinned action/binary by SHA) with an explicit, reviewed allowlist. Cover PSP key material patterns, keystores, tokens and private keys. A finding fails the job; do not suppress wholesale.
- Wire license/notice coverage (`tools/package_notices.py check-coverage` and `check-licenses`) and `repository_check` into the same required job.
- Introduce SPDX/REUSE lint: add `REUSE.toml` mapping first-party files to GPL-3.0-or-later and preserving third-party licenses/notices; pin `reuse` in CI; ensure vendored files keep their own identifiers. No relicensing.
- Extend tests: `tests/test_repository_check.py` dummy-artifact cases, a new `tests/test_reuse.py` (coverage + `reuse lint`), and a workflow assertion that every hygiene gate is present and fail-closed.
- Update `docs/LEGAL.md`/`docs/PROVENANCE.md` with the gate list and how to add a dependency without breaking coverage.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- Dummy `.iso`, `.elf` and `~PSP` staged in a scratch repo are rejected with named errors, locally and in the CI scenario.
- A CC BY-NC-SA component is rejected (existing TC-2.3) and an unlisted `third_party/` file is rejected (TC-2.2) in CI.
- A planted fake secret in a scratch file is caught; a reviewed allowlist entry passes without hiding other findings.
- `reuse lint` is clean; removing a license mapping fails the test.
- Mutation check: disable one gate in a scratch copy and confirm the hygiene test dies for that reason.

**Acceptance / evidence.** Local gate and CI job both block dummy artifacts; secret/license/notice/SPDX gates are required; no real secret or key material is present; docs describe the gates.

**Guardrails.** Never add key material, even as a test value — use clearly fake placeholders. Do not commit third-party binaries. Do not add a gate that only checks for a string while ignoring the actual index.

**Docs.** `docs/LEGAL.md`, `docs/PROVENANCE.md`, `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`, `REUSE.toml`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`.

**Reference projects (hygiene patterns).**
- `Jstar269/hst-decomp` (GPL-3.0) — `REUSE.toml` licensing layout and manifest discipline.
- `zxyandreay/azazel6` (MIT) — `repository_check.py` magic-byte/blob-size/ignore-probe/secret audit.
- `Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp` (GPL-3.0) — notices generated from one JSON source of truth and the CI hygiene matrix.

**Research first (required).** Before writing code, run `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Read the matching source with `gh repo read-file` / `gh repo read-dir`, never raw.githubusercontent.com. Record the references used in the task result; if a reference shapes the design, add a prose note to `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`. PPSSPP, the 3rd Birthday recomp and Metal Gear Acid 2 are behavioral oracles only — never vendored or linked — and a clean-room reimplementation of an existing format, codec or protocol is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0).
Specific first searches: `gh search code "REUSE.toml" --filename "REUSE.toml"`, `gh repo read-file "REUSE.toml" --repo Jstar269/hst-decomp`, `gh search code "gitleaks" --filename "*.yml"`, `gh search issues "REUSE lint vendored"` and `"gitleaks allowlist false positive"`. For the dummy-artifact gate, review `azazel6`/`nakagawa-recomp` repository checks as behavioral references.
result: Hygiene gates landed uncommitted: REUSE.toml (first-party GPL-3.0-or-later default, 9 third_party zone overrides) + LICENSES/ (6 verbatim texts) with test_reuse.py coverage/license/text/zone checks green; CI gains gitleaks (pinned, reviewed path-scoped allowlist), package_notices check-coverage+check-licenses, reuse lint, repository_check; test_ci_workflows.py asserts all gates fail-closed. TC-13.3 scratch-repo cases already covered by test_repository_check.py (run in CI via suite). Mutations (unpinned action, dropped zone, dropped gate) all caught. Gates: ctest 2/2 green, repository_check PASS (446 files). Docs: LEGAL.md gate list + dependency-adding rule, SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md T13d/T13e review. name: Device Vulkan validation layers for diagnosis only
description: Tooling task from the Yakumo review. Steps: stage the arm64 libVkLayer_khronos_validation library plus manifest from local SDK or build trees as TEMP files only, wire a messenger to logcat TEMP, enable validation TEMP on device to diagnose the depth-tested draw issue, then fully revert everything. Run caught one real bug: FIX-white/black resolved color factors no longer need constants, but alpha factors stay CONSTANT_COLOR, so vkCmdSetBlendConstants must still be called whenever either side is FIX (fixed in maybe_set_blend_constants; re-ran to zero validation errors). name: Remove per-frame GPU serialization (waitidle, fence-after-present, overlap)
description: GPU-side follow-up to the CPU frame-path work (9gxichqs, committed as 5b45653). Binding evidence: battle scene holds 20fps with the game issuing ~1 vblank wait per 60 flips (not game-paced), guest worker ~27 percent CPU and main thread ~15 percent visible (neither saturates) — the remaining ~37ms/frame is GPU-side or present-sync, invisible to simpleperf cpu-cycles. Known defects in runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp: render_swapchain_draws calls vkDeviceWaitIdle EVERY frame when calls are non-empty; render_swapchain waits the frame fence again after present; texture upload plus create_draw_resources plus record plus submit are fully serialized with no CPU/GPU overlap. Render structure itself is sane (one pass, ~2700 indexed draws, one submit). Steps: per-frame fence-timestamp or AGI gap measurement first to size the prize; remove the waitidle with proper resource lifetimes (retired-texture reaping already exists — verify it covers the removal); overlap upload/record/submit across frames with in-flight fences; full suite plus repository_check, device proof (fps plus frame-time, scene pixel-identical). Acceptance: measured frame-time drop with no visual change. Blocked on GPU visibility (no Adreno counters on this box) — measure by delta, not attribution.
result: Kept: per-frame vkDeviceWaitIdle and both post-present fence waits removed from swapchain paths; single-flight fence wait now leads render_swapchain_draws before reap/evict/upload. PPSSPP reference: waitidle confined to teardown, never per-frame. Red-first tests/test_gpu_sync.py (3 checks) green; ge_vulkan_tests OK; full ctest + repository_check PASS (432 files). Device (battle snapshot, pid 27746): steady 20.0fps, draws=2677 identical, right-side-only screenshot delta consistent with animation (pre/post RMS 26 localized 1.8 percent pixels vs 7 same-build baseline; geometry path intact). NEGATIVE RESULT: zero fps delta -- renderer was never the limiter; guest produces frames at 20Hz while render thread idles. Bottleneck is producer rate (dispatch/timers/audio), not GPU sync; that is follow-up work, not this task. Uncommitted.

name: T13d — CI build matrix: Linux + Android cross-compile with fail-closed private inputs
description:
Part of T13 (plan §5). Owns TC-13.2 and the `exit 77` contract.

# T13d — CI build matrix and fail-closed private inputs

**Depends on:** T13a.

**Goal.** A clean clone with zero game artifacts builds and tests on GitHub Actions, and a missing private input can never look like a pass.

**Work.**
- Add GitHub Actions workflows (Linux runtime + Android cross-compile) on push/PR: pinned JDK/SDK/NDK/CMake, dependency materialization with digest verification, Linux build + full synthetic suite, Android APK build with the synthetic corpus, `repository_check`.
- Pin every action to a full commit SHA with a version comment; minimum permissions; concurrency cancellation; no secrets; no `pull_request_target` with secret access. Upload only logs/reports, never game frames or generated code.
- Implement the fail-closed private-input contract: CMake `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77` for private-input tests; Python tests honor `GUNGNIR_REQUIRE_PRIVATE_INPUT=1` and turn a skipped private case into a hard failure (or exit 77 where the harness maps it); CI sets strict mode in jobs without game data. Document the convention in `docs/TESTING.md`.
- Prove a clean clone: a job lists tracked files and asserts no `.iso/.chd/.elf/.prx/.bin/.dar/.tpl` or generated corpus; `repository_check` runs on the same tree. No submodules or LFS game blobs.
- Add `tests/test_ci_workflows.py` (red first): workflows exist, actions are SHA-pinned, strict mode is set, Android job uses the synthetic corpus, no secret-bearing triggers, no game paths. Add `tests/test_private_inputs.py` for strict-mode skip conversion.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- Workflow contract test fails before the workflow files exist and when an action is tag-pinned.
- Strict-mode test fails a deliberately skipping private test; non-strict local run still skips cleanly.
- Clean-clone artifact scan fails on a deliberately added dummy `.iso` under a scan fixture.
- TC-13.2: capture the green run on a clean clone and record the run URL/log pointer and the file-count/artifact evidence.

**Acceptance / evidence.** CI is green on a clean clone with zero game artifacts; `repository_check` proves the tracked tree; Android APK built with synthetic fixtures only; private-input tests are fail-closed in CI.

**Guardrails.** Never place game data, keys, driver zips or generated code on runners. Do not require a physical device for CI. Do not weaken a gate to make CI green; fix the cause.

**Docs.** `docs/TESTING.md` (skip contract), `docs/ANDROID.md` (CI build mode), `.github/workflows/*`.

**Reference projects (CI policy).**
- `Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp` (GPL-3.0) — `exit 77` fail-closed skips and synthetic-fixture-only CI.
- `TeamGDB/Yakumo` (MIT) — multi-platform CI/release automation and pinned-dependency jobs.
- `Jstar269/hst-decomp` (GPL-3.0) — toolchain-lock re-verification in CI.
- `zxyandreay/azazel6` (MIT) — `repository_check` merge gate, bounded-run and evidence policy.

**Research first (required).** Before writing code, run `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Read the matching source with `gh repo read-file` / `gh repo read-dir`, never raw.githubusercontent.com. Record the references used in the task result; if a reference shapes the design, add a prose note to `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`. PPSSPP, the 3rd Birthday recomp and Metal Gear Acid 2 are behavioral oracles only — never vendored or linked — and a clean-room reimplementation of an existing format, codec or protocol is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0).
Specific first searches: `gh search code "SKIP_RETURN_CODE" --extension cmake`, `gh search code "exit 77" --filename "*.py"`, `gh search code "android-actions/setup-android" --filename "*.yml"`, `gh search code "gradle/actions/setup-gradle" --filename "*.yml"`, `gh search issues "GitHub Actions SHA pinning"`. Review `nakagawa-recomp` CI and Yakumo nightly automation as behavioral references; never copy workflow text that references game files.
result: CI matrix landed uncommitted: .github/workflows/ci.yml (linux: deps verify, artifact scan, cmake build, ctest, repository_check; android: Temurin 21, pinned SDK 36/NDK 28.2.13676358, build.sh empty-corpus; all actions SHA-pinned, contents:read, no secrets, concurrency cancel, strict env). Fail-closed contract: tests/private_inputs.py helper (skip local/fail strict), probe 0/77 via decide() (SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77 ctest entry), red-first test_ci_workflows.py + test_private_inputs.py green, mutation-checked (unpinned action caught). Docs: TESTING.md skip contract, ANDROID.md CI mode. Gates: ctest 2/2 green, repository_check PASS (437 files). COUNTED GAP (TC-13.2): live green run on clean clone pending -- needs push + Actions observation, not done here; record run URL in follow-up.

name: T10 — Adreno custom Vulkan driver loader
description:

# T10 — Adreno custom Vulkan driver loader

**Depends on:** T9
**Work:** `runtime/platform/adreno/` + Android glue: user picks a driver `.zip` (Mesa Turnip-style Vulkan ICD package) in settings or drops it in a documented folder; extract to app-private storage; validate (entry `libvulkan.so`, ELF machine matches app ABI); load through a custom Vulkan loader that `dlopen`s the ICD instead of the system one (evaluate MIT-licensed libadrenotools vs a minimal own loader — record choice in provenance ledger). Per-driver selection + version display; "system driver" default; fail-closed fallback with a named error. Driver zips/blobs: **user-supplied, gitignored, never bundled** (repository_check excludes the driver directory).
**Test cases:**
- TC-10.1 Stock-driver boot unaffected on any device (loader bypass path).
- TC-10.2 On an Adreno device, a user-supplied zip loads and reports its version via logcat.
- TC-10.3 Malformed zip / wrong-ABI ELF fails closed with clear error, app still boots on system driver.
- TC-10.4 `repository_check` rejects a `.zip`/`.so` committed under the driver paths.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/ANDROID_DRIVERS.md` (what zips are, where to get them, risks, selection UI).
**Refs:** libadrenotools (evaluate), Vita3K/Yuzu-family driver-zip UX (behavioral reference only), nakagawa (`deps.cmake` pin/digest discipline applies to any shim we adopt).
**Gotchas:** §7E.6–E.7.

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): test cases observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Reference snapshot (2026-10-30): ff7ccrecomp's Gradle packaging uses `useLegacyPackaging` and its comment says libadrenotools loads hook libraries from nativeLibraryDir; psprecore's Vulkan context is the host-side consumer. Useful packaging/loading reference for T10.
result:
T10 complete. Adreno custom Vulkan driver loading is implemented, documented and verified on the physical arm64 phone.

TC-10.1 VERIFIED: three consecutive system-driver cold boots on the Adreno phone (Qualcomm Adreno, 3063x1335) and the x86_64 emulator (gfxstream/SwiftShader, 640x320). A selected synthetic package falls back with driver_load_failed; absent hooks and absent private driver directories fall back with driver_hook_library_missing and driver_storage_unavailable; the x86_64 emulator reports driver_abi_unsupported. No partial custom instance is kept.

TC-10.2 VERIFIED: a user-supplied Rutabaga/Turnip zip imports and loads on the phone. Logcat reports driver_active=custom name=rutabaga Mesa driver info=Mesa 26.3.0-devel (git-b00479181d) api=4206951 across three consecutive cold boots. The Qualcomm v863.1 package also loads (Vulkan 1.4.295). The initial failure was our trailing-slash bug: libadrenotools concatenates customDriverDir and soname, while selection.txt writes driver_dir without a slash. The loader now normalizes it; loader_tests asserts the forwarded directory ends with "/".

TC-10.3 VERIFIED: malformed zips produce driver_zip_unsupported, x86_64 ELF produces driver_elf_machine, missing hook libraries and missing/unreadable private directories produce their named fallbacks, and the app still boots on the system driver.

TC-10.4 VERIFIED: repository_check rejects the root drivers/, Android asset driver directory and source jniLibs paths by location, and ZIP/ELF magic catches renamed blobs. Five new probes were red first; .gitignore documents the APK-facing paths. Mutation checks: system path calling custom fails "FAIL: system path never calls the custom opener"; ABI guard removed fails "FAIL: bad_function_call"; retaining the failed custom handle fails "FAIL: failed custom handle is closed".

Documentation and closure: docs/ANDROID_DRIVERS.md covers package sources/risks, both schemas, import/selection UI, private storage, fail-closed troubleshooting, no-bundling, provenance (libadrenotools 8fae8ce2 + liblinkernsbypass aa397589, BSD-2-Clause; miniz 3.1.2 and nlohmann/json 3.12.0, MIT; Volk, MIT; no local patches), named gaps and VERIFIED/HYPOTHESIS/UNSUPPORTED/PLANNED evidence labels. name: Fix per-draw full-texture content hashing (83% CPU)
description: simpleperf 8s battle capture (2026-11-02, pid 5063): 82.77% of all samples in gungnir::ge::Texture::content_key() on guest worker tid 6380. StateMachine::resolve_texture re-reads the full texture (up to 1MB for 512x512x32) from guest RAM and FNV-hashes it byte-by-byte for EVERY draw: 2250 draws/frame at 2.6fps. Keys are runtime-only (snapshots persist regs, never content keys; cache cleared on load), so the hash can change. Fix: word-at-a-time fast hash plus uninitialized read buffer (kills the 1MB zero-fill memset per draw). Semantics unchanged: same bytes still hit the same TextureCache entry. Proof: simpleperf before/after on device battle scene plus guest_frame rate. Follow-up: versioned texture cache with VRAM write tracking (TextureRangeIndex::invalidate_write exists but unwired) if reads still dominate.
result: Word-at-a-time FNV mixer in mix_span (runtime/ge/texture.cpp) plus battle-sized guard test with mutation check (tail-drop caught, reverted). ctest 100 percent, repository_check PASS. Device: content_key 82.77 -> 27.55 percent, guest worker 100 -> 44 percent CPU, 2.6fps (2250-draw battle) -> 20fps (1451-draw scene post-resume). Same-scene battle proof still pending; read+hash still ~43 percent total, follow-up is versioned texture cache (TextureRangeIndex::invalidate_write unwired).

name: T9d — Lifecycle, swapchain recreation, audio recovery and orientation lock
description:
Depends on: T9b.

Make the shell survive the Android lifecycle:
- `onPause`/`onResume` and `APP_CMD_TERM_WINDOW`/`WILL_ENTER_FOREGROUND`: destroy and recreate the swapchain, re-query surface capabilities/format, recreate pipelines only if needed; no use-after-free of `VkSurfaceKHR`.
- Audio lifecycle: attach the existing `AudioSink` to an SDL audio device (or AAudio once T12 lands) with a synthetic tone probe; pause/resume on background/foreground. Actual game audio remains T12.
- Rotation ignored: `sensorLandscape` + `configChanges` so there is no Activity recreate; verify resized surfaces and insets.
- One named error path when swapchain recreation fails; retry on the next resume instead of a hidden crash.

Tests (red first): host state-machine test for pause/resume/surface-lost transitions with a fake surface factory; emulator script backgrounds/foregrounds the app three times and asserts frames continue and the tone resumes; a rotation attempt leaves the UI landscape. Record device evidence (TC-9.4).

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "APP_CMD_TERM_WINDOW" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "vkCreateSwapchainKHR" "out of date" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "Android Vulkan surface lost"`; `gh search code "SDL_OpenAudioDevice" --extension cpp`.

Refs: codepdbh AAudio/lifecycle notes, SDL3 Android lifecycle docs, current T7e swapchain tests, plan §7E.7. Gotchas: §7E.4, §7E.7.
result:
Added VulkanBackend::recreate_surface: wait idle, destroy the swapchain and VkSurfaceKHR, call the stored surface factory, and rebuild the swapchain; the desktop windowed test exercises it before rendering again. SDL background/foreground events are handled in an event watch: background pauses a synthetic SDL audio stream (F32 mono 440 Hz callback), foreground resumes it and requests surface recreation. The main loop retries surface recreation every 500 ms while needed and retries a failed render up to three times instead of exiting.

The shell now forces fixed landscape via SDL_HINT_ORIENTATIONS=LandscapeLeft plus SCREEN_ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE, so it stays landscape even with user_rotation 0. scripts/android/lifecycle.sh runs three background/foreground cycles, requires a new lifecycle_paused and lifecycle_resumed each cycle, checks the final frame is landscape and (when the tone is available) that audio resumed three times.

Evidence: phone (arm64 Adreno) stayed in the same process at 3063x1335 through three cycles with audio pause/resume each time; x86_64 API 37 emulator passed the same gate at 640x320. Full suite 102/102 green; repository_check PASS (260 files).

References used: SDL3 src/video/android/SDL_androidevents.c lifecycle ordering, SDLActivity.setOrientationBis/SDL_HINT_ORIENTATIONS, SDL_AudioStreamCallback/OpenAudioDeviceStream semantics, and the T7e Vulkan backend. Known gaps: fixed LandscapeLeft does not flip 180 degrees; the tone is a lifecycle probe, not game audio (T12).

name: T7f — Vulkan draw path, render-to-texture feedback and GE queue integration
description:
Depends on: T7c, T7d, T7e.

Complete the Vulkan draw path:
- pipelines keyed by blend/cull/depth state; vertex/index upload; texture descriptors; scissor, depth and blend state;
- render-to-texture feedback invalidation (Gungnir's "render to area containing texture" path);
- integrate the GE queue/stall/signal/finish behaviour with command decoding, without stalling on host time.

Tests (red-first): software-vs-Vulkan parity within the documented tolerance; CLUT texture draw; depth/blend/scissor cases; RTT feedback mutation; pipeline-cache identity; no validation errors. Acceptance: all parity fixtures pass on Linux Vulkan and the GE queue no longer completes lists unconditionally.

Specific searches: `gh search code "render to texture" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "GeListUpdateStallAddr" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "VkPipelineCache" --extension cpp`. Refs: codepdbh, sal063, PPSSPP `sceGe.cpp`, Zig-PSP GE queue semantics.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Reference snapshot (2026-10-30): psprecore `Processor::run`/`enqueue` in `runtime/src/ge.cpp` for list queue, stall, SIGNAL/FINISH/END and `runtime/src/platform/gpu_vulkan.cpp` for render-target feedback/cache. Its command processor flushes at the observable points; mirror that discipline.
result: Vulkan draw path: generic mesh pipeline with vertex/index upload, pipeline cache keyed by blend/cull/depth state, texture descriptors, scissor, depth clear/test and multi-draw offscreen readback. Mesh shaders carry clip w and texture q; glslc/embed_shaders.py build both triangle and mesh SPIR-V. Software-vs-Vulkan parity tests cover colour, depth, source-alpha blend, scissor and a CLUT4/8 texture draw; pipeline identity and cull keying are asserted. RTT feedback: TextureRangeIndex tracks guest ranges and invalidates both TextureCache and Vulkan cached textures; a palette-changing re-upload test fails if invalidation is removed. GE queue: hle_media now runs DisplayList instead of completing lists immediately, stops at stall addresses, resumes via sceGeListUpdateStallAddr, carries signal/finish callbacks and logs named decoder failures. Media fixture covers a real stall/resume; boot tests still pass and the boot runner links gungnir_ge. Full suite 69/69 green; repository_check PASS. References used: psprecore ge.cpp/gpu_vulkan.cpp/display_vulkan.cpp/soft_renderer.cpp/texture.cpp/vertex_pipeline.cpp (MIT), PPSSPP sceGe.cpp/GPUCommon.cpp/ge_constants.h, KanaStation ge.cpp, Zig-PSP GE types, SDL3 Vulkan API.

name: T8a — TPL decoder and format facts
description:
Depends on: T3, T7 (parent T8).

Decode the PSP TPL containers Gungnir ships: 0x30-byte header (magic,
version, n_tex), per-texture H/W/BW/bpp/data_off entries, 4bpp swizzle,
8bpp+CLUT, pixel formats 0-7. Expose one runtime API that returns decoded
RGBA8 texels plus the facts dump/replacement need (dimensions, bufw, bpp,
swizzle, CLUT bytes, source guest range). DXT formats 8-10 are decoded only
if fixtures require them; otherwise they are recorded as a named gap, never
silently mis-decoded.

Write docs/formats/TPL.md from the user's local files at layout level only:
offsets, field meanings, swizzle rule, CLUT layout. No TPL bytes, no game
textures, no dump hashes in the repository.

Tests (red first, synthetic fixtures of our authorship):
- TC-8.1 decode half: synthetic containers decode to hand-computed pixels.
- TC-8.4 edge cases: odd widths, multi-texture n_tex > 1, bpp=4 alpha ramp,
  bpp=5 CLUT decode.
- Malformed header/offset/data_off cases fail with named errors.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code
"<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete
implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"`
for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "tpl" --extension cpp`; `gh search code
"texture swizzle" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "palette 16" --extension
cpp`; `gh search issues "PSP texture swizzle"`; `gh search code
"texture_collection" --extension cpp`.

Refs: psprecore `runtime/src/gpu/texture_collection.cpp` and `texture.cpp`
(MIT, behavioral reference), gungnir-ptbr TPL/DAR facts, PPSSPP texture
decode behavior (diff oracle only, never linked). Gotchas: §7B.2-B.4, §7F.3,
§7F.4 (bpp=5 CLUT layout).
result:
Added runtime/tex/{tpl.hpp,tpl.cpp} and the gungnir_tex target. Decodes the n_texture/table header, 0x14-byte texture descriptors (H/W/BW/pixel-format/data offset plus preserved opaque bytes), 8-byte palette descriptors and swizzled CLUT4/CLUT8 data through the shared T7d GE texture decoder. Palette CLUT masks derive from entry count; RGB565/RGBA5551/RGBA4444/RGBA8888 palettes supported. 0xFFFF auxiliary entries are counted in Tpl::resources with bounded sizes and never silently dropped. Named failures cover truncated tables, bad offsets, unsupported formats (DXT/0x0108), invalid dimensions, partial swizzle geometry, invalid palettes and missing CLUT palettes. Tpl::bytes and raw descriptor bytes are preserved for the T8b writer.

Tests: tests/tex/tpl_tests.cpp (built by tests/test_tpl.py) covers synthetic CLUT4 alpha ramps at odd width, RGB565 and RGBA8888 palettes, CLUT8, multi-texture containers, resource counting and malformed inputs. Mutation check: fixing the CLUT mask at 16 entries fails 'CLUT mask selects all 256 entries'. Full suite 76/76 green; repository_check PASS (216 files). Local ASan/UBSan scan of the user's extracted TPLs decoded 1,886 textures / 58,952,576 pixels from 1,304 of 1,305 unique containers; only debugFont.tpl (pixel format 0x0108) fails closed and is recorded as a named gap in docs/formats/TPL.md.

References used: kreycai/gungnir-ptbr tools/fonte_gungnir.py and docs/graficos_com_texto.md (header fields, 4bpp swizzle, alpha-ramp palette), local header inspection of INI.DAR/DATA.DAR (table/palette layout, multi-texture and 0xFFFF resource sentinel; no bytes copied), marco-calautti/Rainbow TPLTexture.Serializer.cs (structurally comparable multi-image TPL only; it is the Nintendo format, not the Gungnir PSP variant), LiinkPK/Texture-Replacement-Tool-for-PPSSPP (binary-only replacement UX for T8c/T8d, no source adopted), PPSSPP PR #8715/wiki (textures.ini semantics for T8c/T8d), PPSSPP image-formats doc (GE TPF numbering).

name: GE swapchain blend constants
description: The swapchain draw loop never calls vkCmdSetBlendConstants (headless loop does), so FIX-factor draws render unlit on device; swapchain also has no depth buffer while headless does. Scope: mirror the headless constants call + audit depth parity in render_swapchain_draws; extend the FIX Vulkan parity test to cover the swapchain builder path (shared create_draw_pipeline already carries mask+constants state). References (behavioral only): runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp headless vs swapchain loops; pspsdk GU_FIX semantics. Red-first: FIX parity case fails without the call; device screenshot shows lit (not washed) world. Proof: host headless scene render + device screenshot.
result: vkCmdSetBlendConstants now called on both headless and swapchain loops via shared maybe_set_blend_constants helper (covered by FIX parity test). Shipped in device build; terrain still black so constants were not the cause - see follow-up terrain task.

name: GE render targets (FBP per draw)
description: Track the guest draw buffer (FBP 0x9C / FBW 0x9D, ZBUF 0x9E/0x9F) per draw; render into per-target surfaces; composite the display buffer (sceDisplay framebuffer) on flip; sample GPU targets for render-to-texture reads. Scope is structural: DrawState.target already captured, needs surfaces + display select + invalidation via existing TextureRangeIndex. References (behavioral only): highcmd/chinatown-wars-psp-recomp runtime/src/ge_render.cpp current_target(), fboTexAddr RTT sampling; BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp runtime/src/rt/ge.c ge.fbp/fbw + guest-VRAM writes. Red-first: draws to two different FBP addresses land on different surfaces (host test); no-target-switch scenes render identically. Findings 2026-11-02: corpus is single-target (all draws FBP 0, all 43 texture addrs in RAM, no RTT) so routing is a proven no-op (byte-identical renders); RTT sampling on software path (exact RGBA8888 match), GPU RTT named gap; display select via sceDisplay offset with legacy render-all fallback.
result: Done and committed as 75846de. TargetSet routes draws by FBP offset into per-target software surfaces with display select on flip (sceDisplay offset, target 0, first surface); Vulkan present paths filter to the display group with legacy render-all fallback; software RTT sampling on exact RGBA8888 match, GPU RTT named gap. Red-first: targets unit tests red on stubs, display-target Vulkan parity red (mashed image). Full suite green, repository_check PASS. Regression: corpus is single-target FBP 0 with RAM-only textures (no RTT), so routing is a proven no-op (byte-identical host renders across 4 same-moment runs); PPSSPP side-by-side keeps layout with known fade delta; device battle fully playable post-change.

name: T10b — Host-side driver package inspector and extractor
description:
Depends on: T10a.

Add `runtime/platform/adreno/package.{hpp,cpp}`: inspect and extract a user-supplied driver zip into app-private storage without loading it.
- Read and validate `meta.json` (`schemaVersion`, `name`, `libraryName`, `minApi`, `vendor`, `driverVersion`); accept a plain `libvulkan.so` package only if T10a records that shape.
- Validate the ICD ELF before extraction: ELF64, little-endian, `ET_DYN`, `EM_AARCH64` for `arm64-v8a`, non-empty `.dynsym`, sane size caps.
- Reject zip-slip (absolute or `..` paths), duplicate/overlong entries, encrypted or unsupported compression, and entries over the size/count budget.
- Extract atomically to a staging directory then rename; stable per-driver id; idempotent re-import; delete. Every rejection is a named error; no silent skip and no partial install.
- Use a pinned library for zip/JSON (miniz MIT / libzip BSD-3 / an existing JSON dependency); never hand-write the container or JSON parser. Record the choice and license in `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`.

Data: `DriverPackage {id, display_name, vendor, driver_version, min_api, soname, staged_dir}`; `scan_drop_folder()` and `remove()`.

Tests (red first): synthetic zips authored by the test (stored + deflated), a Turnip-shaped `meta.json` package, a plain `libvulkan.so` package, missing/bad `meta.json`, zip-slip, duplicate names, entry-count/size cap, wrong ELF class/machine (`EM_X86_64`, 32-bit), truncated ELF, missing soname. Fixtures are generated bytes; no real driver binary is committed.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "ZipFileReader" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "EM_AARCH64" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "miniz" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "zip slip"`; `gh search code "libadrenotools" --extension cpp`.

Refs: PPSSPP `UI/DriverManagerScreen.cpp` (meta.json install flow), libadrenotools `tools/ADPKG.md`, Vita3K `android_driver.cpp`, T9 Android storage. Gotchas: §7A.7, §7E.6.
result:
Added runtime/platform/adreno/package.{hpp,cpp} and a host driver_package_tests suite. The inspector reads a whole zip snapshot, computes the content id as the first 16 hex of SHA-256, validates every entry name (absolute/.. /control/overlong), duplicates, entry count, per-entry/total/archive budgets, encryption and compression support, parses meta.json with nlohmann/json, and validates the ICD as ELF64 LE ET_DYN EM_AARCH64 with a non-empty .dynsym via <elf.h>. Both package shapes are accepted: Turnip-style meta.json with required schemaVersion 1, name and libraryName (soname must name a root .so), or a bare libvulkan.so with exactly one root library. All failures are named: driver_zip_missing/unsupported/slip, driver_entry_duplicate/oversize/name/encrypted, driver_meta_invalid/schema/name, driver_library_missing/ambiguous, driver_elf_class/machine/type/truncated/dynsym, driver_storage_unavailable, driver_id_invalid.

install_driver_zip extracts the same validated snapshot into filesDir-style drivers/<id>/.staging-<id> and renames only after every entry is written; re-import of the same id is idempotent and remove_driver is idempotent. scan_drop_folder returns valid packages plus per-file named errors (case-insensitive .zip). ZIP is handled by miniz 3.1.2 (MIT), JSON by nlohmann/json 3.12.0 (MIT), both vendored byte-identical and pinned with tree digests in dependencies.json; provenance and the SOURCE_PROVENANCE library table were updated. No driver binary or zip is committed.

Tests synthesize zips with miniz and ELF64 headers with no real driver. Coverage: stored+deflated entries, both package shapes, metadata/schema/name/minApi/vendor errors, zip-slip including a patched absolute name, duplicates, overlong names, archive/entry/total/count limits, encrypted and unsupported-method entries, ELF class/machine/type/truncated/empty dynsym, install/re-import/remove, scan sorting/errors, and no staging directory after a failed install. Mutation evidence: disabling the encryption guard changes the encrypted fixture's named error; disabling the path guard accepts zip-slip; both kill the suite for the intended case. Full suite 114/114 green; repository_check PASS (285 files); deps.py verify passes for all eight entries.

References used: gh search code "ZipFileReader" --extension cpp (PPSSPP and other zip reader call sites); gh search code "mz_zip_reader_init_mem" --extension cpp (miniz API usage); gh search code "EM_AARCH64" --extension cpp (ELF machine checks); gh search code "miniz" --extension cpp; gh search issues "zip slip" (path-traversal and extraction-budget failure reports); gh search code "adrenotools_open_libvulkan" --extension cpp (loader call sites). Upstream miniz 3.1.2 release, nlohmann/json v3.12.0 release assets, <elf.h> definitions.

name: T16 — Widescreen rendering: 16:9 and ultrawide
description:
Widescreen rendering: let the 3D scene use the whole phone display at 16:9
and wider, with 2D content (HUD, menus, subtitles) undistorted and FMV video
pillarboxed rather than stretched.

Why. The PSP renders 480x272 and the host fits that rectangle into the
display with letterboxing (`runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp:358`,
`fit_viewport`). On a 19.5:9 phone that is a small picture with large bars.
Most PSP widescreen work is a per-title memory patch, but our pipeline owns
the world/view/projection multiply (`runtime/ge/vertex.cpp:264`) and the
viewport mapping (`vertex.cpp:426`), so widening can be host-side and needs
no guest cheat engine.

Scope.
- A `widescreen` mode in the host config and the Android intent extras:
  off, display aspect, and a 16:9 cap (use the display aspect). Off is
  bit-identical to today.
- Widen the projection for perspective draws only; orthographic and
  screen-space draws (HUD, menus, text, pixel-pinned effects) keep their
  480x272 mapping. Full-screen 2D effects (fades, vignettes, letterbox
  bars) stretch with the scene so no unfaded strips appear.
- Fill the presentation target instead of pillarboxing when the widened
  scene matches the display; FMV/PSMF video stays in its native box.
- Per-title override for a game-specific projection constant or draw
  exclusion (source path still to be decided; see T16a).
- Record the mode in the snapshot config identity (T15) so a snapshot
  cannot load into a differently configured session.

Out of scope. Widening the guest framebuffer or its 512-pixel stride; the
guest still sees 480x272. Guest-side frustum culling also stays as the game
does it, so geometry outside the unwidened frustum stays missing.

Risks to settle while implementing: depth-tested edge effects that read
pixels (RT64 added `gEXVertexZTest` for exactly this), culling that assumes
the 4:3 frustum, and scenes that render to a 480-wide texture first (a hard
limit that must be detected and counted, never papered over).

Decomposition (dex): T16a (projection widening for true widescreen) and T16b
(fill-screen presentation: stretch/crop/fit). Their research steps are
`Research first — T16a` and `Research first — T16b`.

Status 2026-11-03: research complete for both subtasks; implementation not
started. Code-grounded review (see the subtask descriptions) corrected two
plan assumptions:

- 480x272 is 1.765:1, already almost 16:9 (483.6 px at 272 height), so a
  "16:9" host mode is a 0.7% change and visually identical to off for this
  title. The real win is the display aspect (19.5:9 -> 604 px virtual,
  k = 1.26). Keep 16:9 as a cap for other titles.
- T16b is NOT independent of T16a: both edit `fit_viewport`,
  `scale_scissor_to_extent`, their two call sites, `VulkanBackend::Config`
  and the intent extras. Land T16b first and let T16a consume its policy.

Two PSP recompilations add a third widescreen option to T16a: The 3rd
Birthday hooks the game's camera entry points and passes the window aspect
so the game widens and culls itself, then squeezes only the HUD; Chinatown
Wars keeps fit/letterbox and scales the HUD instead. Their full-screen-quad
heuristic is adopted inside T16a; the camera hook is rejected because it
needs per-title RE.

name: GE fog
description: Implement PSP fog (0x1F/0xCD/0xCE/0xCF): fog color + near/far, applied in vertex/pixel path for transform-mode draws. Scope: decode into DrawState, software rasterizer + Vulkan (push-constant fog uniforms), parity test. References (behavioral only): highcmd/chinatown-wars-psp-recomp runtime/src/ge_render.cpp (p.fog, fogColor); BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp runtime/src/rt/ge.c (vertex+pixel fog). Red-first: fogged-quad fixture fails before, passes after. Regression check 2026-11-02: post-fog event render is byte-identical to pre-fog (fog factors all 1.0 on current corpus: end=20000/slope=1e-4), PPSSPP side-by-side in /tmp/opencode/scene/vs-ppsspp-fog.png shows the known cream-wash delta persists and is NOT fog (fog color is dark blue); that wash is tracked by later GE tasks.
result: Done and committed as a29fe39. Fog decoded (0x1F/0xCD/0xCE/0xCF) into TransformState (per-vertex factor, through=1, inf/nan end handling) and DrawState (enable+color, clears/through off). Software interpolates linearly and mixes 256-denominator; Vulkan fog varying + push-constant enable/color at offset 32, pipeline-keyed. Red-first: fog_decode (2 failures), fog_mix (1 failure), Vulkan parity (1 failure after software landed) all observed before fix. Event (643/799) and battle (1317/1718) frames enable fog but factor is 1 everywhere (end=20000/slope=1e-4), so identical renders, no regression. Suites green, repository_check PASS.

commit.message: Implement PSP fog across vertex, software and Vulkan paths

name: T11b — Touch overlay and editable layout
description:
Depends on: T11a.

Touch overlay (native Android View):
- Add `runtime/input/touch_overlay.*` (C++ layout/pointer/edit/JSON model, host-tested) plus a thin `com.gungnir.recomp.input.TouchOverlayView` for Canvas drawing and MotionEvent handling above the SDL surface in landscape. The View asks the model for a pixel snapshot and forwards touches through JNI.
- Controls: floating analog stick (appears under the thumb, follows drags), 8-way d-pad, four face buttons, L/R and START/SELECT. Respect safe-area insets and multiple simultaneous pointer ids; show pressed visuals.
- Track each pointer by id and role so a finger can slide between controls without sticky buttons; release every pointer on ACTION_CANCEL, focus loss and background.
- Editable layout: a Layout/Reset control in the Activity toggles edit mode; drag moves a control, resize changes its radius, positions clamp to the safe screen, reset restores the default. Persist a versioned JSON layout in app-private storage with an atomic temp-file+rename. Missing/corrupt/older layouts fall back to the default with a named log; never crash the overlay.
- Publish the merged touch state to T11a through a JNI `nativeTouchState(buttons, x, y)` call; the C++ core stores it as the Touch source. Make `InputState` thread-safe because the View runs on the UI thread while HLE reads on the SDL thread.
- Host tests: C++ contracts for layout defaults/hit-testing, pointer-id tracking, stick and d-pad deflection, slide-between-controls, drag/resize clamping, JSON round-trip, schema/version handling, corrupt-file fallback and atomic file storage.
- On-device: overlay appears over the app, presses reach the JNI touch state, layout edits survive restart. Haptics are T11c, not this subtask.

Reference set: **TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, pinned b61852a)** is the primary behavioral source — `profiles/mhp3rd/host/input/touch_controls.*` (floating stick, `dpad_buttons`, `stick_deflection`, finger roles), `ui/touch_editor.*` (drag/resize/reset) and `tests/touch_controls_tests.cpp`; port the semantics to the C++ model, copy no code, and record provenance. Behavioral references only (GPL; no code or assets copied): PPSSPP (`UI/TouchControlLayoutScreen.*`, pointer capture/analog drag), Dolphin (Android input overlay/hide), RetroArch (overlay hit-testing), Flycast (Android virtual gamepad), reVC/re3 (mobile touch UX). Platform contract: Android `View`/`Canvas`/`MotionEvent`/`WindowInsets` and app-private file I/O.

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): tests observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "touch_controls" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "touch_editor" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "virtual joystick" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "Android touch overlay drag resize"`.

Device validation: see `android/AGENTS.md` — emulator is for initial bring-up; physical arm64 phone QA is required at sprint end and recorded in `docs/qa/`. Reproducible emulator: `scripts/android/emulator.sh`.
result:
T11b complete (implementation 1fe90b3, QA 3c0c2c6).

- runtime/input/touch_overlay.*: host-testable layout/pointer/edit model. Defaults for floating stick, 8-way d-pad, Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle, L/R, Start/Select; safe-area-normalized placements; pointer roles by id with slide-between-controls; floating stick origin follows past reach; edit drag/resize clamps to the safe box; reset. Versioned JSON (version 1) with Older/Corrupt statuses that leave the previous layout intact.
- runtime/input/touch_layout_store.*: writes a sibling .tmp then renames over the target; missing/older/corrupt are named, a failed write removes the temp and leaves the previous file. A load error is reported as corrupt rather than missing.
- Android: com.gungnir.recomp.input.TouchOverlayView draws a pixel snapshot with Canvas and forwards MotionEvents through JNI; Controls button toggles edit, long-press resets; onPause/focus-loss release and save. Drivers button moved bottom-right so it no longer covers R. SELECT label shortened to SEL to fit.
- JNI publishes the touch mask/analog through the T11a InputState. InputState now has a mutex because the View is on the UI thread and HLE reads on the SDL thread. Touch gestures route to edit_* while editing; touch_up now ends an edit drag.
- Red-first: tests/input/touch_overlay_tests.cpp and tests/test_touch_overlay.py were added before touch_overlay.* existed; the first configure failed on the missing touch_overlay.cpp, then the contracts went green. The suite covers hit-testing, multi-touch, slide, stick clamp, d-pad diagonals, edit clamp, JSON round-trip, version/corrupt fallback and atomic store round-trip. Final suite 135/135; Android clean-checkout APK gate passes; repository_check PASS (318 files).
- Device QA on M2102K1AC (arm64, API 34), app 1fe90b3: overlay draws; temporary JNI diagnostics observed touch_down buttons=0x4000 (Cross); Cross/stick/d-pad visuals verified; Cross moved to cx=0.7389886379/cy=0.6332540512 and survived force-stop/restart; long-press reset restored cx=0.82/cy=0.74/radius=0.05; corrupt file logged touch_layout_corrupt_default and defaulted; three cold boots FRAME_OK at 3063x1335 on the system Adreno driver. Report docs/qa/2026-10-31-t11b-touch-overlay.md.

References: TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, pinned b61852a) touch_controls.* and ui/touch_editor.* for floating-stick, dpad_buttons/stick_deflection and drag/resize semantics (port, no code copied); PPSSPP touch-layout/pointer capture, Dolphin Android overlay, RetroArch hit-testing, Flycast virtual gamepad as behavioral references only (GPL, no code or assets copied); Android View/Canvas/MotionEvent/WindowInsets contract. Gaps: touch haptics are T11c; overlay hide on gamepad is T11d; game/synthetic-fixture navigation is T13.
